Now it is a composite. So, beer is available now has gone up by about 2,000 outlets or 3,000 outlets

items.statement: Karnataka additional excise duty rolled back from Rs 1,050 to Rs 750-800 per case for affordable beer
items.quote: Now, they rolled it back to about Rs. 750 - Rs. 800.

items.statement: Lost 4-5% market share in Karnataka (from ~17.5-18% to ~12.5-13%); recovered 1% in July; expect further recovery in Q2-Q3
items.quote: Yes, we have roughly lost about 4 % - 5% and we have recovered 1% of that. The trend is showing that 1% is possible to gain and 2% - 3% is possible in this quarter, I think. It is possible.

items.statement: UBL growth driven by Andhra Pradesh where SOM is not present; SOM tender pending in AP
items.quote: for example, they have Andhra Pradesh. Last year, they had a problem due to the route to market in Andhra Pradesh. This year, they worked in zero base in Andhra Prades h. So, the growth is coming from there. Mukund Agarwal: Okay. Diwakaran S.: And we are not present there. Our tender is pending

items.statement: Inducted independent directors with good repute to improve corporate governance
items.quote: And it is our endeavor to have good corporate governance, and we are working towards it. That is why we have got, we have inducted independent directors who have got good repute in the market.

items.statement: Child labour issue pertained to private limited company; no pending litigation; company claims it was unnecessarily targeted
items.quote: So, there is number one, as we have given out press release, also it pertains to our private limited company. And I think nothing has come out of it. I think it was, I mean, we were unnecessarily targeted. So, as of now, there is nothing about it.

items.statement: Beer realization Rs 566 per case in Q1, up from Rs 550 in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Beer realization stood at Rs. 566 per case, up from Rs. 550 in Q1 FY25.

items.statement: Premium beer segment growing at 25-30%; Woodpecker targeting 12-15% of market
items.quote: Almost 12 % - 15% of the market is growing at 25 % - 30%. And in that market is where Woodpecker is playing.

items.statement: Telangana re-entry under consideration but lower priority than Andhra Pradesh due to profitability concerns
items.quote: Yes, it is in the cards and we are constantly in touch with the government there and the authorities. But in terms of priority, I w ould rather get it to AP first than Telangana , because Telangana continues to be not very profitable for the existing business.

items.statement: Bangalore airport T2 and T1 brand visibility effort underway; expect execution in 6-8 months
items.quote: There is an effort to set up there in T2 and T1. There is an effort, we will do it sir. We can do it in the next 6 months - 8 months.

items.statement: Single Malt whisky in pipeline; premium IMFL focus over next 3-4 quarters
items.quote: We have a few more premium SOM Distilleries & products in the pipeline, including a Single Malt. I think that is where the growth is going to lie in the next three quarters to four quarters

items.statement: Completed Rs 381 crore rights issue and Rs 911 crore preferential issue in Q1FY26
items.value: Rs 381 crore rights issue and Rs 911 crore preferential issue
items.quote: On capital raise, as S hachin mentioned, we successfully completed Rs. 381 crores of rights issue and are in the process of Rs. 911 crores of preferential issue this quarter

items.statement: Announced Rs 1,400 crore all-cash acquisition of Profectus Capital with AUM of Rs 3,468 crore as of March 2025
items.quote: We have announced a Rs. 1,400 crore all -cash acquisition of Profectus Capital which is progressing well. Shareholder approval is secured and change of control and allied regulatory approvals are underway.

items.statement: Expect disbursement momentum to pick up from Q2FY26 as seasonal effects subside
items.quote: Looking ahead, we expect disbursement momentum to pick up from Q2 as seasonal effects subside.

items.statement: Target embedded finance to be 10-12% of total AUM in next 2-3 years
items.quote: We would like to be around 10% to 12% of the total AUM.

items.statement: Aim to increase emerging market contribution to 35% of portfolio by end of FY26 from 22% at March 2025
items.quote: Our emerging market business at end of March '25 was about 22% contribution to the overall portfolio. And we want to take it to around 35% by end of the year.

items.statement: Foresee yields to go up by 0.25% to 0.5% in coming year due to mix shift
items.quote: So, we foresee the yields to go up by 0.25 % to 0.5% in the coming year.

items.statement: Target steady state ROA of 4% in next 6-8 quarters with Profectus acquisition and operational leverage
items.quote: And we have talked about that earlier as well, is that at a steady state, we want to reach 4% ROA levels with Profectus acquisition and operational leverage which we are getting.

items.statement: Expect ROA to increase by 0.2% to 0.3% each quarter on steady state basis in interim period
items.quote: In the interim for about a year, it would increase on a steady state level. Each quarter about 0.2% to 0.3%, that is what the estimate is.

items.statement: Expanded emerging market footprint from 150 locations in FY24 to 309 locations as of June 2025
items.quote: In this journey, we have expanded our footprint from 150 locations in FY '24 to 309 locations as of June '25.

items.statement: Emerging market network near full rollout with 286 operational branches by June 2025 and clear path for more expansion by September 2025
items.quote: Our emerging market business expanded to 286 operational branches by June with a clear path for more expansion by September 2025.

items.statement: 121 of 286 emerging market branches have broken even; others on path to break even in next 12-15 months
items.quote: So, out of total 286 branches, 121 branches have already broken even and others in next 12 months to 15 months are on the path of breaking even.

items.statement: Internal estimate: stabilized branch can deliver Rs 1-1.1 crore monthly disbursals at Rs 20 lakh ticket size and 18% yield
items.value: Rs 1 crore to Rs 1.1 crore per month
items.quote: And broadly, our internal estimate is that a branch should be able to deliver Rs. 1 crores to Rs. 1.1 crores of disbursal per month once it becomes stabilized, with a ticket size of Rs. 20 lakhs with a yield of 18%.

items.statement: AUM closed at Rs 12,081 crore, up 31% year-on-year
items.quote: Now on business update, our AUM closed at Rs. 12,081 crores, up 31% year -on-year.

items.statement: Disbursements for Q1FY26 were Rs 1,599 crore vs Rs 1,146 crore in Q1FY25; sequential decline from Rs 2,436 crore in Q4FY25 was by design
items.quote: Disbursements for the quarter were Rs. 1,599 crores compared to Rs. 1,146 crores in Q1FY'25, the sequential decline from Rs. 2,436 crores in Q4 FY '25 was by design and in line with our budgets.

items.statement: Embedded finance crossed Rs 1,000 crore AUM milestone; disbursed Rs 582 crore through MyShubLife platform with monthly run rate of Rs 100-150 crore
items.quote: In Embedded Finance, we crossed the milestone of Rs. 1,000 crores AUM this quarter. We disbursed Rs. 582 crores through MyShubLife platform with a monthly di sbursal run rate of between Rs. 100 to Rs. 150 crores.

items.statement: Total income grew 40% YoY to Rs 421.8 crore; net total income grew 31% YoY to Rs 216.5 crore; PAT up 12% YoY to Rs 34.1 crore
items.quote: Our total income grew 40% year-on-year to Rs. 421.8 crores. Our net total income stood at Rs. 216.5 crores, a 31% year -on-year growth. Our PAT came at Rs. 34.1 crores for the quarter, up by 12% year -on-year.

items.statement: ROA excluding branch expansion impact at 2.3% in Q1FY26, in line with internal estimates
items.quote: ROA for Q1FY'26, if we exclude the branch expansion impact, would be at 2.3%, which is in li ne with our internal estimates.

items.statement: GNPA at 2.5% and Net NPA at 1.7% in Q1FY26, well within internal estimates
items.quote: Portfolio quality stayed intact with GNPA at 2.5% and Net NPA at 1.7% well within our internal estimates.

items.statement: Unsecured portfolio witnessed stress from over-leveraging; tightened underwriting and curtailed disbursements to Rs 186 crore in Q1FY26 from peak Rs 623 crore in Q2FY25
items.quote: Our unsecured portfolio though has witnessed some stress on account of over -leveraging. As mentioned earlier, we have tightened our underwriting and have curtailed disbursements in last two quarters. (Rs. 186 crores in Q1FY '26 vs peak Rs. 623 crores in Q2FY '25).

items.statement: Credit cost was Rs 47.7 crore in Q1FY26, up 44% YoY but lower than Q4FY25's Rs 54.3 crore
items.quote: Our credit cost was Rs. 47.7 crores, representing a 44% year -on-year increase, but lower than Q4FY'25, which was Rs. 54.3 crores.

items.statement: Emerging market vintage branches (>18 months) have GNPA 2.4% and credit cost ~1%; newer branches (<18 months) have GNPA 0.2% and credit cost 0.3%
items.quote: Our GNPA for vintage branches is at this point in time 2.4%, well within the estimates and for newer branches , it is 0.2%. Similarly, for credit costs, for greater than 18 months, the average credit cost is about 1%. For newer branches at this point in time, it is 0.3%.

items.statement: Profectus Capital maintains gross NPA of 1.6% and net NPA of 1.1% as of March 2025
items.quote: Profectus has demonstrated stable portfolio expansion, building its access under management to Rs. 3,468 crores as of March 2025 with presence across 7 states through a 28-branch network and over 800 member teams, all while maintaining a gross NP A of 1.6% and a net NP A of 1.1%.

items.statement: Total debt at Rs 7,586 crore as of June 30 with over 50 lenders; long-term rating A+ with positive outlook from India Ratings
items.quote: Total debt at Rs. 7,586 crores as of June '30 and with over 50 lenders, we have a very diversified liability profile. Our long-term rating is A+ rating watch with positive implications, assigned by India Ratings.

items.statement: Cost of borrowing 150-200 bps higher than peer set due to high growth rate; aim to reduce cost of borrowing even if it means moderating growth
items.quote: One of the biggest input to our ROA journey, which is less in our control is our cost of borrowing. Our cost of borrowing vis-à-vis our peer set has remained elevated. It's roughly around 150 to 200 basis point more than most of our peer set.

items.statement: New co-lending guidelines allow first loss cover to banks which could lower co-lending cost and improve ROE
items.quote: Second big positive is that, RBI for the first time has allowed first loss cover to be given to the bank. Now, some people think, how can that be good? I will tell you why it is good. So, today, if any state bank of India or a large NBFC is a co-lending partner, they have to take, carry the risk of the total co-origination based co-lending which they do. Now, because of that, they charge a certain

items.statement: New co-lending guidelines bring all co-lending under regulatory umbrella; expect 2 quarters of disruption from January but volumes should multiply thereafter
items.quote: My view is that from January to two quarters, there would be disruption to reset the new process. The biggest of the challenges would be that now we have to select our co-lending partner at the point of origination itself. I don't think so the technology is a challenge because in most, at least in o ur case, with most of the banks, we are fully integrated both in simultaneous lending and post disb

items.statement: Portfolio LTV at 55% at portfolio level; prime secured loans up to 80% LTV on self-occupied residential, commercial, industrial properties
items.quote: So, at a portfolio level, our loan-to-value would be around 55%. While for prime secured loans, we go up to 80%. But at a portfolio level, this would be about 55%. And we do self -occupied residential property, commercial property, industrial property.

items.statement: Embedded finance targets small/medium retailers using payment ecosystems (PhonePe, BharatPe, Paytm); daily repayment product with average ticket <Rs 2 lakh
items.quote: Typically, this is a daily repayment product and not a monthly EMI product with an average ticket size of less than Rs 2 lakhs.

items.statement: UGRO is 100% business loan company; only lends to Udyam Aadhar registered MSME customers; no buy-now-pay-later or personal loans
items.quote: No, we do not do buy now, pay later. We do not do PL. UGRO is a 100% business loan company. We only give loan to a Udyam Aadhar registered MSME customer.

items.statement: Elevated Anuj Pandey to CEO; Shachindra Nath to focus on strategic initiatives, investor/lender interface, organic/inorganic growth
items.quote: This quarter, we also elevated Anuj as our CEO. He has been with me since UGRO's very inception. When we started UGRO, the organizational design was to have a CEO for the business so that I can focus on strategic things which are investor interface, lender interface, organic and inorganic business growth opportunity and CEO can focus on core operating performance.

items.statement: CFO Kishore and Amit exited; Shilpa Bhatter elevated from Deputy CFO to CFO as pre-planned succession
items.quote: On CFO again, it's a personal choice. Obviously, a CFO role in UGRO is a difficult role. If you look at the banking financial services industry, majority of the easy lending from mainline banks is to entities which have either have a parent or have a vintage. And sometimes, UGRO has a very deep diversified lending base. So, you have to not only interact with the global DFI, you have to interact wi

items.statement: Industry facing higher stress in certain unsecured segments; UGRO exposure limited and ring-fenced with tightened underwriting
items.quote: The industry is currently facing higher stress in certain unsecured segments, but our exposure there is limited and ring -fenced. Approximately 70% of our book is secured and our underwriting filters are sharper than ever.

items.statement: Anticipate certain market pockets will show stress; proactively pivoted asset engine as a measure
items.quote: Our continuous endeavor has been to deliver consistent growth, consistent performance, but we continue to believe that certain pockets of the market would show some amount of stress. We have been anticipating that and we have pivoted some of our asset engine accordingly as a proactive measure.

items.statement: Expects Q2 revenue and profitability to be substantially higher than Q1 sequentially
items.quote: Sequentially also, we are looking at very, very healthy growth in revenue and profitability.

items.statement: Projects healthy double-digit revenue and profitability growth for engineering services in FY26
items.quote: As I previously guided, we project very healthy double-digit growth in revenue and profitability for this business unit in this fiscal.

items.statement: Targets finance cost as percentage of revenue to return to 3.xx% range in next 2 quarters
items.quote: We can commit to you that, that is definitely not a number that you're going to see next quarter. You will see it get below that to 3.xx, and we will maintain it at that.

items.statement: Targets working capital days to reduce from 76 to 60 days long-term
items.quote: We believe that the long-term potential steady state, that is about 60 days.

items.statement: Expects Raebareli plant utilization to reach 70% in Q2 and 80% by year-end
items.quote: We are at 65%. I think in the next quarter, we hit 70%. Our goal is to hit 80% by the end of this year.

items.statement: Committed to double-digit revenue and profitability growth long-term across 5 prioritized BUs
items.quote: We are committed to double-digit growth in revenue and profitability over the long term.

items.statement: PEB order backlog strong and growing with INR200 crore order from JSW and INR300+ crore from Reliance
items.quote: We have received a INR200 crores order from JSW. We've received from Tata Electronics. We performed in excess of INR100 crores, INR150 crores, I think, INR157 crores. So, Reliance has been in excess of INR300 crores.

items.statement: Body-in-White secured new clients including Hyundai, Sears Automotive, TIVOLT, Ashok Leyland
items.quote: We had mentioned last time that we now have -- other than Stellantis, we have Hyundai, we have Sears Automotive, we have TIVOLT, Ashok Leyland, and there are several others also that are coming in.

items.statement: Boilers and process equipment order backlog grown strongly to INR110 crores with further additions expected
items.quote: Order backlog has grown strongly to INR110 crores, with further additions expected.

items.statement: US PEB order backlog at USD54 million with strong active order backlog indicating strong Q2
items.quote: Order backlog is good. So, we maintain something called an active order backlog, which is a very good lead indicator for what our revenue for the next quarter is going to be.

items.statement: PBT margin at 4.75% in Q1 due to labor issues, expects improvement in Q2 as mix shifts to higher-margin businesses
items.quote: Our PBT margin for the first quarter stands at 4.75%. Again, the impact of our -- the labor issues that we had in our revenue being not what we were expecting initially has resulted in some amount o f margin contraction here, but a very, very temporary issue pertaining to about a month or 2

items.statement: India PEB margins 200-300 bps below competitors on PBT basis, working to improve
items.quote: Our PEB India margins are lower than our competitors. So, we are hard at work trying to get that up. We are about 200, 300 basis points less than our competitors on a PBT basis.

items.statement: Raebareli plant commissioned with 20,000 tons/year capacity, INR300 crore revenue potential at 80-85% utilization
items.quote: Raebareli firing on all cylinders gives us INR300 crores of revenue.

items.statement: US hydraulics faces 50% tariff from August 27, making cost structure not viable, redirecting volumes to Europe, Canada, Australia, New Zealand
items.quote: The upcoming 50% tariff, which is set to be effective August 27, well, it makes the cost structure not really viable. So, it could affect our US sales. Our mitigation plans are in place, and we are redirecting volumes to Europe, Canada, Australia and New Zealand.

items.statement: Working capital days at 76 in Q1, higher than planned due to labor issues, expects meaningful improvement in Q2
items.quote: Working capital days currently stands at 76. This is higher than planned, again, the same labor issue that I had mentioned.

items.statement: Finance cost at 4.16% of revenue vs guided 4%, expects to return to 3.xx% in next 2 quarters as working capital normalizes
items.quote: The overall finance costs as a percentage is 4.16%, while we have guided you to 4%. These are due to the delayed dispatches that we had at Raebareli plant and due to the lower revenue, which are now behind us.

items.statement: Targets debt-equity at 0.6-0.7 and interest cost at 3.xx% of revenue long-term
items.quote: All of that will come with keeping our debt equity at the 0.7, 0.6 number, keeping our overall interest cost as a percentage of revenue at the 3.xx number is the way we intend to manage this company.

items.statement: US tariff changes affect hydraulics exports (2.2% of revenue), 50% tariff effective August 27
items.quote: I do want to guide that this revenue stream represents about 2.2% of Pennar's entire revenue. So we do not, on an overall basis, expect a significant impact.

items.statement: PEB revenue 40% of total, focused on manufacturing and engineering companies like JSW, Tata Electronics, Reliance
items.quote: If you include our India and US revenue, about 40% of our overall revenue for the company is metal buildings and pre-engineered buildings and high-rise buildings.

items.statement: Views new PEB listings positively, expects added discipline on margins and capital efficiency
items.quote: I think it's a very good thing for these listings. And I see it as a massive plus point because when you are listed, I think there's a higher degree of -- margins become important.

items.statement: Labor supply constraint in Q1 caused INR100 crore revenue loss, resolved by mid-June with expanded labor pool from West Bengal, Orissa and more contractors
items.quote: I think we have lost close to INR100 crores in revenue in Q1 because of that.

items.statement: ROCE at 22.3% using EBIT/(total assets - current liabilities), evaluating inclusion of short-term borrowings
items.quote: Now in relation to ROCE, we've always used a definition of EBIT divided by capital employed. We've been in touch with some of you. We've been talking to our investors and discussing this internally.

items.statement: ROE at 12.12% annualized for Q1, projects improvement through the year
items.quote: Our ROE, of course, will remain unchanged calculation-wise, and it's at 12.12% for the quarter annualized, and we project improvements on this in the course of this financial year.

items.statement: PEB India order book near INR855 crores, US PEB at USD54 million, both trending upward with INR200+ crores new orders booked recently
items.quote: The order book now stands at USD54 million and India PEB order book close to INR855 crores.

items.statement: Expects margin improvement as portfolio mix shifts to higher-margin businesses (PEB, Body-in-White, boilers, engineering services)
items.quote: We absolutely expect our margins to improve well once our portfolio mix shift to higher-margin businesses continues.

items.statement: Other expenses increased INR37 crores in Q1 (INR26 cr standalone: erection, subcontract, spares; INR11 cr subsidiaries: acquisition-related legal/professional), expects moderation in Q2-Q3
items.quote: Other expenses increased by INR37 crores. The variance is predominantly account of -- in stand-alone by INR26 crores, which comes through higher erection expenses, subcontract expense and spare consumables.

items.statement: Y-o-Y total revenues and total income declined 10.4% to INR 661 crores due to U.S. tariff uncertainties
items.quote: our Y-o-Y total revenues and total income saw a decline of 10.4% and stood at INR 661 crores versus INR 738 crores during the same quarter last year. This is largely on account of the uncertainties that prevail owing to the tariffs that have been imposed by the United States.

items.statement: Spinning utilization at 99%, Sheeting at 60%, Terry at 68%, largely range bound with minor realization fluctuations
items.quote: Our capacity utilization levels were largely range bound during the quarter, as you might have seen already, the Spinning was at 99%. The Sheeting division came in at 60% and Terry at 68%, pretty much the same as last quarter, some minor fluctuations in realizations.

items.statement: Proposed additional 25% U.S. tariff creating uncertainty; strategy reinforced to expand global client base into other jurisdictions and channels
items.quote: The proposed additional 25% tariff to be imposed by the United States has created some uncertainties and has adversely impacted sentiments. And this environment reinforces our strategy of expanding our global client base into other jurisdictions, geographies and channels.

items.statement: Opportunities seen in UK following India-UK FTA signed July 2025; initiatives will take months to formalize
items.quote: We see opportunities to expand our market presence in the UK following the signing of the FTA between India and the UK in July 2025. Of course, for initiatives on the UK front to come to fruition, it will take a few months until the agreements are formalized and effective.

items.statement: India market revenue streams growing Y-o-Y across three brands (Himeya, Atmosphere, Liv) covering broad price points and categories
items.quote: We continue to see Y-o-Y growth in our revenue streams from our India market.

items.statement: On track for 2030 sustainability goals; initiatives to fast-forward deadline to rationalize energy costs
items.quote: On the ESG front, there's really no change from the last quarter, and we remain on track to achieve some of our key sustainability goals by 2030. We are also taking initiatives to fast forward this deadline of 2030 that we have set internally for ourselves, which will also help us rationalize some of our energy costs.

items.statement: Net debt reduced to INR 2,405 crores from INR 2,425 crores at March 31, 2025
items.quote: During the first quarter, we continued to bring our debt down vis-à-vis March. Our net debt stood at INR 2,405 crores versus INR 2,425 crores during the end of March 31, 2025.

items.statement: India business expected to close to double from previous fiscal; targeting INR 800-1,000 crores over next few years
items.quote: We expect our India business -- India business to close to double from the previous fiscal. And we seem to be broadly on track vis-a-vis our vision of taking India to close to INR 1,000 crores, INR 800 crores to INR 1,000 crores over the next few years.

items.statement: Servicing 35 non-U.S. jurisdictions and over 70 non-U.S. clients; priority to expand presence in non-U.S. jurisdictions
items.quote: We currently service 35 non-U.S. jurisdictions. And we are taking and making additional efforts to enhance our presence across these jurisdictions to reduce some of our dependence on the U.S. given the volatility.

items.statement: Up to 25% tariffs not seen as material challenge; India 5% better than China, 6% worse than Pakistan; wait-and-watch on tariffs above 25%
items.quote: We believe that up to 25% of tariffs shouldn't create any material disturbance or any stir of any kind or any interruption of any kind because we will be comparable to other competing home textile geographies such as China and Pakistan.

items.statement: No clients have pulled back orders or asked to stop production; clients in wait-and-watch mode on tariffs above 25%
items.quote: The customers have not -- as we speak, we haven't seen any clients pull back on any orders nor have we seen any clients ask us to stop production at this point.

items.statement: No specific plans to relocate manufacturing facilities due to regulatory limitations and asset constraints
items.quote: There are limitations in doing so, Survankar, because of the underlying regulations and the assets that are involved in the process. So we don't have any specific plans of relocating any manufacturing facilities at this point.

items.statement: EBITDA margin band 18-22% shared as model expectation, not FY26 guidance; 150-200 bps tariff impact share expected on first 10%
items.quote: As far as margins is concerned, we have shared with stakeholders earlier that our EBITDA margin band is 18% to 22%, and that's where we believe our model should deliver. That's not a guidance for '26, but that's more a band guidance that we believe we should be at, at any given time.

items.statement: First 10% tariff phase: clients shared some burden, rest absorbed by retailers or passed to consumers; 10-25% bucket to follow similar pattern with slightly lower impact
items.quote: we expect 150 basis to 200 basis point share somewhere in that range. And of course, it's dependent on product mix. And we had also said that as far as the first phase of 10% went, the clients have reached out on sharing some of the burden on tariffs, and we said that we will share a little bit of burdens of the total.

items.statement: No conclusive discussions on 25-50% tariff bucket; unprecedented situation being digested; wait-and-watch mode
items.quote: The last 25 to 50 bucket, there has been no discussions yet because quite honestly, it's been just a week since it's been imposed. And everybody is just digesting how to handle an uncertainty and a phenomenon of this nature, which is unprecedented and sort of as far as India is concerned, and we haven't seen something as absurd as this before.

items.statement: No order cancellations for Himatsingka; media reports on cancellations may cover other categories like apparel
items.quote: There is no such things as client cancelling orders of Indian exporters. That's a broad and sweeping comment, Bhavin. I cannot say that nothing has occurred. I can say that nothing has occurred vis-à-vis Himatsingka.

items.statement: Brands used as total solution providers, not to mitigate B2B risk; margin impact neutral (100-200 bps max); brands add value in India, e-comm, Qcom channels
items.quote: we use, at least as far as Himatsingka is concerned, brand portfolios to optimally position ourselves as total solution providers and make sure that we are available to clients with a more holistic portfolio of solutions than without it.

items.statement: U.S. revenue share ~60% and reducing; target below 50% in 18-24 months in normalized scenario
items.quote: pure U.S. should be in the region of 60% going south. Over the last 2 fiscals, it has corrected substantially because of our Terry division ramping up in other jurisdictions as well and so on, plus our foray into India and things like that. So 60% and reducing.

items.statement: Himeya brand at 3,500-4,000 points of sale; Liv brand targeting 10,000-12,000 points of sale; expanding across bedding, bath, drapery, upholstery
items.quote: Our footprint for our Himeya brand is in the region of 4,000 -- around 3,500 to 4,000 points of sale. And we intend to take our Liv brand to over 10,000, 12,000 points of sale at this point.

items.statement: Revenue loss from key customer exits (BBB) and brand recalibration caused headwinds; growth appears sluggish due to making up lost revenue
items.quote: we were also unfortunately in a position where we had to face revenue loss because of key customers that were not part of our portfolio anymore vis-à-vis BBB and things of that nature. And we also had to face revenue loss on account of brand recalibration.

items.statement: Capex program concluded except annual organic needs; 2-year timeframe to optimize utilization to high 90s and deliver ~INR 4,000 crores revenue within 18-22% EBITDA band
items.quote: we believe that in a 2-year timeframe, we were looking at essentially sweating our capacities, and we felt that we should be able to optimize our utilization levels, take it to the high 90s and be in a position to deliver revenues of approximately INR4,000 crores and stay within our EBITDA band of 18% to 22%.

items.statement: Other expenses down 30% Y-o-Y due to brand cost reduction; expected to remain range bound unless unusual tariff-related events
items.quote: We believe it should be range bound. It's reflective of some of the reduction in brand costs and things of that nature. So we believe, Nirav, that this -- I mean, this proportion should be range bound now unless there is an event of some kind as a result of these tariffs, which causes us to enhance certain expenditure.

items.statement: Full-year FY26 EBITDA margin target of 18% average, with FY27 target of 19-20%
items.quote: Yes, we definitely expect it to grow from the current 13.3% levels to an average of 18% for the full year and we are quite confident of that both in the domestic and international market.

items.statement: FY27 EBITDA margin target of 19-20%
items.quote: If we are expecting 18% for the full year, we are confident that next year this will improve further and believe margins in the range of 19% to 20% are achievable going forward.

items.statement: Total FY26 capex of Rs. 150 crore including Rs. 25-30 crore maintenance capex
items.quote: The maintenance CAPEX is expected to be Rs. 25 to Rs. 30 crore and the total CAPEX to be around Rs. 150 crore.

items.statement: Rs. 60 crore investment plan in Thailand under implementation
items.quote: For the future, we have a Rs. 60 crore investment plan in Thailand which is under implementation.

items.statement: Ranchi expansion 70% commissioned, full completion by end of Q2 FY26, adding 40,000 tons overall capacity including 20,000 tons rope capacity
items.quote: As of now, we have already installed about 70% of the capacity and the remaining 30% installation will be completed by end of Q2, around October.

items.statement: Sizable US tender secured providing strong order visibility for rest of FY26

items.statement: Genome Valley formulations facility under Granules Life Sciences completed first-ever FDA pre-approval inspection July 28 to August 1 with single procedural observation; response to be submitted within timeline
items.quote: A key milestone was achieved at our new formulations facility at Genome Valley under Granules Life Sciences, which underwent its first-ever FDA pre-approval inspection from July 28th to August Ist. This was successfully completed with a single procedural observation, and the response will also be submitted within the stipulated timeline

items.statement: Genome Valley facility unlocks additional 10 billion doses formulations capacity, a 40% increase over existing 26 billion dose capacity at Gagillapur; establishes second source supply of finished dosages and PFIs to US from India

items.statement: Expect FY27 as very good growth year starting from last quarter of FY26; Gagillapur remediation clearance expected by December 2025; Genome Valley approval expected in 35-40 days; real growth to start after approvals

This is for FY26.

items.statement: Management expects opex to remain almost stable in absolute terms, increasing only by the rate of inflation.

items.statement: Management expects to receive another INR100-150 crores from ARC in coming quarters.

The market is brutally competitive at this point of time, and eve rybody is fighting for price because of large underutilized capacities at various players

items.statement: FY26 handover guidance of 3,300-3,600 units and revenue of INR 1,250-1,300 crores

items.statement: Q1 FY26 sales volume 0.82 msf, value INR 441 crores, up 17% YoY

items.statement: Q1 FY26 collections INR 338 crores, highest ever Q1
items.quote: collections at INR 338 crores is the highest in any Q1 so far and is driven by healthy sales handover and milestone linked receipts.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 EBITDA INR 47 crores at 18% margin

items.statement: Q1 FY26 construction spend INR 111 crores, new project investment INR 75 crores
items.value: INR 111 crores construction; INR 75 crores new projects

items.statement: Pune debut project Codename Superstar sold 150+ units (36% of launch supply) in first 4 weeks

items.statement: Kolkata project Shriram Springfield approvals in place, pre-sales overwhelming, launch imminent

items.statement: Target to double project pipeline over 18-24 months; 20+ msf under evaluation
items.quote: Further projects with 20+ million square feet at various stage of evaluation across core markets. This wider funnel provides option value and a multiyear runway, allowing us to stay selective while still aiming to double the upcoming pipeline over 18 to 24 months.

items.statement: Gross debt INR 567 crores, net debt INR 380 crores, net D/E 0.28; no significant debt increase expected

items.quote: Gross debt stood at INR 567 crores, down from INR 646 crores in March 2025 with a net debt of INR 380 crores. Our net debt-to-equity ratio of 0.28 among the lowest in the sector.

items.statement: Price hikes limited to 1-3% in micro markets; era of double-digit hikes over
items.quote: During the quarter, we would have seen couple of percent increase, 1% or 2% in some micro markets and 2% to 3% in other micro markets. So the prices are not going anywhere this year.

items.statement: End-user demand resilient in mid/mid-premium segments; Chennai revival, Bangalore supply-driven recovery
items.quote: Underlying demand remains strong. I don't think a huge momentum loss is there, at least in our core markets of Bangalore, Chennai, even in Pune that we have seen. I n fact, it has picked

items.statement: Government royalty decision expected soon; path clear but timeline uncertain
items.quote: As I said in my May call, we think we have made a meaningful progress. The final decision outcome is expected. As is with any government, it is expected any time, but it has not come through for the last couple of quarters.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 handovers 740+ units, highest ever Q1; FY26 target 3,300-3,600 units
items.quote: Over 740 units have been handed over to customers, again, highest ever Q1 number for SPL.

items.statement: JV/DM projects contributed 46% of Q1 handovers; ~1,000 JV units targeted for FY26
items.quote: Our JV portfolio also contributed meaningfully with a profit share of INR 5 crores, representing 46% of total handovers in Q1 coming from JV projects.

items.statement: Added 1 Bangalore project GDV INR 200 crores in Q1; 6 projects (3 msf) nearing closure Q2-Q3; 5 projects (3+ msf) advanced commercial closure H2

items.quote: During Q1, we added 1 project in Bangalore with GDV of INR 200 crores within a short period of acquisition, approval process has started ahead, and it is expected to launch in H2 FY26. 6 projects totaling 3 million square feet are nearing closure. 5 projects totaling around 3+ million square feet of projects are at an advanced stage of commercial closure.

items.statement: ASK platform has INR 135-140 crores remaining investment scope; new fund discussions underway
items.quote: We already have at least scope for another INR 135-140 crores of investment that can be made from the existing platform itself. We are working towards deploying that soon.

items.statement: No significant IT layoff impact seen; GCC growth compensating; demand contraction only if IT sector collapses
items.quote: We don't think there will be a demand contraction in the near future, unless the IT sector collapses. Then, there will be a confidence crisis in the minds of customer and that might lead to.

items.statement: No immediate plan to increase promoter holding; SEBI-approved inter-promoter transfer in progress
items.quote: There is no immediate plan to increase promoter holding. As you know, there's a transaction which is already approved by SEBI and it is in the working, in terms of inter promoter transfers.

items.statement: Royalty savings ~INR 4 crores annually (5% of PBT) as brand usage phased out
items.quote: Annually, we have incurred about 5% of PBT in the past, which is about INR 4 crores or something that was the number the annual run rate we had in the past couple of years. To that extent, we'll save during this year.

items.statement: Q1 was difficult with continuing softness in consumer demand aggravated by trade working capital pressure from cooling products slowdown in April-May, recovery only in June
items.quote: Q1 was a difficult and challenging period. There was a continuing softness in consumer demand, which was aggravated by pressure on trade working capital owing to the slowdown in cooling products, especially in April and May, and it was only in June that we saw some recovery.

items.statement: Product business grew double-digit in both volume and value in Q1 FY26
items.quote: Overall revenues grew by 9.9% on the back of a double -digit growth in our products business. This growth was driven by a double -digit volume growth in both our key categories of EWPs and VCs.

items.statement: Economy and premium EWP segments grew strongly; robotics vacuum cleaners grew 52%
items.quote: We saw 52% growth in robotics, and this helped drive the vacuum cleaner category to strong double-digit growth.

items.statement: Service bookings grew double-digit driven by AMC count growth, ASP increase, and higher multi-year booking mix
items.quote: We had a healthy double -digit growth in fresh service bookings. This growth came from a combination of growth in AMC count and an increase in the ASP. We also saw an increase in the number of multi-year bookings.

items.statement: Expect double-digit service bookings growth to sustain in coming quarters
items.quote: As we look ahead at the periods ahead, we feel very confident that we will see double -digit growth in service bookings sustained and all the efforts that we've made and that we continue to put in, in service transformation, picking up pace and helping us drive growth.

items.statement: Service bookings growth to reflect in reported revenue from Q4 FY26
items.quote: In terms of impact in the P&L, you can expect to see the numbers show up in the reported numbers by Q 4 of this year.

items.statement: Adjusted EBITDA margin at 11% in Q1 after higher service charge payouts and growth investments; PAT grew 24.1%
items.quote: On the profitability side, the adjusted EBITDA margins for Q1 came in at 11%, after accounting for higher service charge payouts and with the increased growth investments. Our profit after tax grew by 24.1% over last year.

items.statement: Gross margin at 59.7% in Q1, range-bound vs 60.5% last year; tactical promotions impacted margin
items.quote: Our Q1 gross margins at 59.7% were range bound versus 60.5% last year and 20 basis points higher on a sequential basis. Commodity costs remained benign for most parts. Given the challenging market conditions in the quarter, tactical promotions were run, which led to a gross margin drop.

items.statement: Expect gross margins to remain range-bound with multiple levers including product-service mix, price points, and cost management
items.quote: We bel ieve that our structural advantages and guardrails on gross margin in the form of a healthy product and service mix, portfolios straddling various price points and effective cost management, give us several levers on gross margin

items.statement: Aim for full-year margin improvement in FY26, not pushed to FY27
items.quote: There should be absolutely no doubt whether the margin expansion agenda is being pushed to FY 27, certainly not. It very much remains part of the ambition for FY 26.

items.statement: Filter manufacturing done in-house at Dehradun and Bangalore factories with abundant capacity for foreseeable growth
items.quote: All our manufacturing of filters, et cetera, is done in-house. We have 2 factories, as you know, one in Dehradun, one in Bangalore, and it's all done in-house. We have abundant capacity to accommodate for filter growth in the foreseeable future.

items.statement: Expanding service network of partners and technicians is ongoing work stream as category penetration grows
items.quote: Expanding our service network and growing the service capacity is an ongoing work stream that will continue in the foreseeable future. items.statement: Launched 2-year filter life EWPs across economy to premium segments; now have over 40 such products

We now have more than 40 products that offer two -year filter life.

items.statement: Scaled up smart IoT-enabled premium EWP range in Q1
items.quote: In the premium segment of EWPs, we scaled up our smart IoT-enabled range during the quarter.

items.statement: Market share unchanged despite increased competitive activity; new entrants validate category potential
items.quote: You'll be happy to know that notwithstanding the increased competitive activity, our market share has not gone down. It's remained absolutely unchanged, and we feel confident about that going forward as well.

items.statement: Vacuum cleaner category growth expected to surpass 17% CAGR projection; robotics momentum accelerating
items.quote: Vacuum cleaner category, it talks about the category becoming Rs. 1,500 crores by FY 30 from Rs. 500 crores in FY 23 at a CAGR of 17%, as you can see on the slide 20 , of our IR pack I can tell you that with robotics going the way it is, we are seeing that momentum already being surpassed and we expect that to sustain going forward.

items.quote: We strengthened our engagement with our business partners and our service technicians and rolled out direct payouts to the technicians, along with performance-based incentives.

items.statement: Non-cash ESOP charges at Rs 5.6 crore in Q1, expected to remain at these levels in FY26
items.quote: Non-cash ESOP charges were Rs. 5.6 crores and are expected to remain at these levels in FY 26.

items.quote: On the operating cost also, definitely, the operating cost will rationalize and it will be within the guidance that we have given of around 6.2%.

items.quote: We are quite confident that in terms of growth and in terms of credit cost, both we will be able to outdo the guidance. But before revising, we will watch out 1 or 2 more quarters.

items.quote: During the quarter, our net interest margins have also improved to 11.5%, which were around 10.9% in Q4.

items.quote: If you look at as a percentage of overleveraged customers in terms of more than 2 lakh exposure, it has come down to just 1%.

items.statement: Surface Express utilization maintained at 82% despite volume softness; peaked at 83.5% last year; target 83.5-84% with volume recovery

items.statement: Q1 FY26 EBITDA Rs. 33 crore, margin 11.5% vs 10.5% Q4 FY25 and 12% Q1 FY25; PAT Rs. 21 crore, margin 7.3%

items.statement: Receivable days 58, payable days 35, net working capital cycle 23 days consistent with historical performance

items.quote: Margins in Surface, Air Domestic and Rail are all more or less equal and slightly less in Air International business because this is a very competitive business and is a high -volume business basically.

items.quote: On sustainability, on other sustainability side or you can say like grain logistics, we are piloting EVs for last mile and mid -mile operation in selected cities and implementing renewable energy solution, including solar rooftop at newly built up these three sorting centers.

items.statement: Marketable Molecules full-year EBITDA margin expected higher than last financial year

items.statement: Distribution channel grew 8.6% in Q1; online channel declined 8% due to warehouse transition disruption
items.quote: Our operational revenue grew by 1.2% year -on-year to INR 343 crores in Q1 FY '26, largely benefited by higher distribution, which has registered a growth of 8.6% and growth in large format stores, while the online channel had a de -growth of 8%.

items.statement: July sales recovered and Q2 is on track per internal budgets
items.quote: Without like diverging into numbers, I can share with you that we have recovered in terms of the sales in July and we expect a decent quarter too. We are basically in line with our budgets, like internal budgets, what we have aligned.

items.statement: Gross margin expanded 210 bps YoY to 55.4% driven by premium mix and cost efficiencies
items.quote: We also saw an improvement in our gross margins, which expanded by 210 basis points, Y-o-Y from 53.3% to 55.4%.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved 10 bps YoY to 15.9%; PAT margin declined to 6.4% due to higher depreciation
items.quote: Our EBITDA for Q1 FY '26 was INR 55.4 crores. The EBITDA mar gin stood at 15.9% during the quarter, an improvement of 10 basis points versus last year. PAT stood at INR 22.2 crores during the quarter and PAT margin stood at 6.4%.

items.statement: ASP increased 14.7% YoY to Rs 671 driven by sneaker premiumization and scaling down low-margin entry products
items.quote: This highlights our commitment to premiumization while ensuring competitive pricing even amidst macroeconomic headwinds. We continued to enhance our product portfolio by launching over fifty new value-for-money styles across men's, women's and children's categories.

items.statement: Sneaker category grew 150% YoY to 550,000 pairs; sneaker saliency now 50%+ of portfolio
items.quote: Notably, our sneaker category achieved a remarkable 150% growth, we sold 550,000 pairs versus 2 20,000 pairs last year, reinforcing our dedication to providing stylish, high-quality footwear at accessible prices.

items.statement: Consciously scaled down DIP school shoes, slippers and sandals at entry price points with lower-than-average margins
items.quote: Secondly, there was, we did slow down on the lower margin, lower MRP, DIP school shoes and some bit of sandals and slippers, which were not very margin accretive and very, very low value.

items.statement: New raw material warehouse capacity 200,000 pairs/day vs previous 80,000 pairs/day; de-bottlenecks supply chain
items.quote: Now, the new warehouse gives us a capacity of, in a mature state and a high-throughput state, we can easily go up to 200,000 pairs a day. So, it is basically doubling of the capacity of the throughput.

items.statement: Commenced in-house upper production at Paonta Sahib facility from 1st August 2025
items.quote: As we speak, we have further augmented the in -house manufacturing capacities for upper by commencing the production of upper at our Paonta Sahib facility in Himachal Pradesh starting 1st August 2025.

items.statement: Haridwar II facility now up and running at full scale for sneaker production
items.quote: Of course, we should not be comparing it versus last year but now this 500,000 pairs to 700,000 pairs would become a base for every quarter because our Haridwar II facility is also now up and running at full scale.

items.statement: Non-BIS inventory proportion significantly reduced; gross margin improvement reflects lower liquidation impact
items.quote: The proportion has significantly reduced. And that, again, has started reflecting in our gross margins as well. So, on the one side, there is a ASP increase and on the other side, there is a cost efficiency, which means that now we are getting lower hit in terms of liquidation of non-BIS inventory and all, as compared to same quarter last year and as compared to last quarter as well.

items.statement: BIS regulation benefits starting to materialize; non-BIS inventory liquidation deadline June 2026
items.quote: The regulation says that everyone has to dispose off the inventory before June 2026. So, everyone is taking their time to do that. But that is not really a big issue now with anyone as the overall inventory is , I believe, finite and not that significant.

items.statement: Intense price competition from unorganized players at lower price points; company taking mitigation steps
items.quote: Yes, that is true. Actually, on the ground, a lot of the unorganized players are, you know, cutting prices a lot. And, there is intense competition on ground.

items.statement: Held largest-ever distributor meet SHOECASE 2025; conducting 150+ retailer meets across country

The feedback we received for our latest Focus collection has been overwhelmingly positive, enhancing our growth visibility and raising hopes for demand recovery in the upcoming quarters.

items.statement: Collected distributor orders through December; strong secondary sales traction in North and West markets
items.quote: We have basically been, you know, executing apart from this one issue that we had on the warehouse. We are executing very well on the front-end side. And we are currently doing, we have had a fantastic distributor meet where we have collected orders till basically December. We have a very high visibility of the order pipeline.

items.statement: Warehouse consolidation and SAP implementation caused 15-20 day online sales disruption; revenue impact estimated Rs 10-12 crore

And I mean, had everything been normal and we would have shown a bit of growth there as well. So, it would have an impact of maybe around Rs. 10 crore to Rs. 12 crore of revenue there, which on an overall basis would have added maybe 3%, 4% growth.

items.statement: Women's segment and South geography identified as key growth drivers
items.quote: Of course, product, sneakers, and from a category perspective, like segment perspective, women's share is another driver. And from a geography perspective, South is the driver.

items.quote: So, the secondary growth -- while the primary growth in the franchisee sale is 34%, secondary is 24%, which effectively same around which I said 80%, 85%.

items.quote: As per the plans, we always believe in giving you a conservative estimate and an approach. And so, from that perspective, we have always said that we want to open 18 to 20 stores every year, year-after-year, funded by the profits, funded by the equivalent amount of debt that we have. items.statement: Management expects minimum 20-25% top-line growth for FY26 and EBITDA margin to normalize to historical 12.5-13% range

items.statement: Order book stands at Rs 5,147 crore to be executed within next three years

items.statement: Received new orders of Rs 1,851 crore in FY25, including Rs 1,134 crore rail projects

items.statement: Bidding pipeline currently at Rs 3,000 crore; annual bidding volume of Rs 10,000-12,000 crore
items.quote: Our current bidding pipeline is Rs. 3000 crores and the team is working on the same. When railway projects are floated, we will bid more. This is the current pipeline. But we are bidding more or less Rs. 10,000 to Rs. 12,000 crores a year.

items.statement: Jal Jeevan Mission extended to 2028 with budget provisions, increasing likelihood of payment releases
items.quote: The Jal Jeevan Mission program has been extended by the Central Government until 2028 with provisions made in the Union Budget. This increases the likelihood of payments being released for the works executed by the company.

items.statement: Railway capex of Rs 2.52 lakh crore for FY26 creates substantial civil and core infrastructure opportunities
items.quote: With a capital allocation of ₹2.52 lakh crore for the fiscal year, the government is focusing on projects such as expansion, electrification, redevelopment, and safety enhancement. These initiatives are expected to create substantial opportunities in civil and core infrastructure projects.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 EBITDA margin at 11.54%, down from historical 13-13.5% due to higher employee costs at new sites and interest burden
items.quote: EBITDA margin reported at 11.54%.

items.statement: Management expects EBITDA margin to normalize to historical 12.5-13% range as receivables improve
items.quote: Last year it was 12.5%, 12.6% or 13%. In between, this range it will maintain.

items.statement: Receivables declined marginally from Rs 735 crore (Mar'25) to ~Rs 700 crore (Jun'25); received Rs 400+ crore in Q1 from MP, UP, Rajasthan
items.quote: Current receivables are marginal decline from what they were in March'25. Last March'25 was Rs. 735 crores. And currently it is around Rs. 700 or Rs. crores.

items.statement: Expect receivables to normalize in 6-8 months; >50-60% of stuck payments to be released by March 2026
items.quote: We are expecting that it may take six to eight months now to get into the normal level.

items.statement: Total debt ~Rs 700 crore (unchanged from Mar'25); promoter unsecured loan increased from Rs 59 crore to Rs 110 crore (interest-free); trade debt reduced from Rs 350 crore to Rs 300 crore
items.quote: The debt was increased, but now we have promoters fund in the company. We have decreased our trade lines. Earlier, it was around Rs. 350 crores in March. This is now around Rs. 300 crores. But promoters have infused funds in the company through unsecured loans. Therefore, it is showing at the same level.

items.statement: Debt-to-equity at 0.9x; management aims to maintain current leverage level
items.quote: We have already started to reduce the debt. But it is in the reasonable ratio already, less than 1, it is around 0.9 times.

items.statement: Steel structure and grader plants operating at full capacity; fleet gross block Rs 250 crore (WDV Rs 180 crore) fully utilized
items.quote: Our steel structure and grader plant are operating at full capacity. With these three manufacturing facilities, we are able to reduce project costs without compromising on quality.

items.statement: Geographic concentration reduced: Rajasthan share down from 65% to 47%; now operating in 12 states with 14 state government clients
items.quote: Earlier, my concentration in Rajasthan was 65%. Now, in today's date, my concentration is only 47%. We have expanded to other states.

items.statement: Water supply 76% of revenue (TMI), railways up from 12% to 18%, roads steady at 6%
items.quote: The main project is the water supply project, which has received about 77% of the company's revenue in previous year and around 76% during the current TMI period.

items.statement: Railway revenue contribution increased to 18% in current period from 12% in FY25
items.quote: The railway sector contributed around 12% to the company's revenue in the previous financial year, and during the current PMI period, its contribution has increased to about 18%.

items.statement: Historical order win rate 16-18%; maintained across segments
items.quote: Our historical success ratio is between 16% to 18% every year.

items.statement: On-time project delivery rate exceeding 90% in Q1 FY26
items.quote: In terms of the project execution, we achieved an on-time delivery rate exceeding 90% despite industry-wide challenges supported by efficient deployment of manpower, machinery, and materials.

items.statement: Higher finance costs and slower receivables recovery impacted net profit (down 53% YoY) despite 8% revenue growth and 5% EBITDA growth
items.quote: Net p rofit for the quarter stood at around Rs. 7 crores, which has declin ed by 53% year-on-year basis. PAT margin for the quarter stood at 2.57

items.statement: Central government share of Jal Jeevan Mission payments expected soon; state governments releasing funds in parts
items.quote: The central government share is about to release soon and as soon as that arrives, the entire liquidity is going to release in the coming time.

items.statement: Payment delays from government (21-22 months) increased working capital, reduced turnover 16% in FY25 vs FY24
items.quote: Due to the delay in the payment of the work done, the company has recorded a 16% decline in financial year 2025 compared to the financial year 2024.

items.statement: Receivables accumulation of last 21-22 months will take 6-8 months to normalize even with payment releases
items.quote: It is the accumulation of last 21, 22 months. It is not going to reduce in one month, two months or one quarter. We are expecting that it may take six to eight months now to get into the normal level.

items.statement: Company exploring ETP/STP projects; recently started STP project in Jaipur (municipal); researching industrial ETP opportunities
items.quote: Recently, we also got the work of STP in Jaipur. We started it. We are also trying in the same way in ETP, sir.

items.statement: Guides FY26 revenue growth of 12-15% and EBITDA margin around 23%
items.quote: So I think overall, yes, from a company perspective, we still guide for about 12% to 15% overall, given that the glassware business is growing pretty well.

items.statement: Confirms FY26 EBITDA margin guidance of ~23% including other income
items.quote: I think for this year, you should look at an EBITDA margin of around 23-odd percent for the entire year.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 gross margin hit record 54%; EBITDA margin 24%, PAT margin 14%
items.quote: For the quarter, we have achieved the highest ever gross profit margin at 54%, reflecting our manufacturing excellence, strong positioning as a premium brand in the market and enduring relationships with our distributors and channel partners.

items.statement: Glassware plant at 65% efficiency, dragging EBITDA by ~100 bps for FY26; breakeven expected by year-end
items.quote: So the idea is that we have to be breaking even by the end of the year in this particular segment, which we anticipate we will be able to do given reducing cost and rising revenue trends in this particular segment.

items.statement: Unable to raise prices in April due to aggressive competition; energy and wage costs increased
items.quote: And ideally, we -- every year, we kind of raise prices in April. But unfortunately, we were unable to do that this year, given that there was very aggressive pricing by a lot of competition for this quarter to try to gain traction in sales.

items.statement: Consumer demand recovery not yet full; early rains hit hydration sales in May
items.quote: Having said that, we are yet to experience a full consumer demand recovery across categories. The growth has also been hit by a slightly earlier onset of rains, particularly in May and -- which affected the hydration category, which saw dip in sales in that particular month.

items.statement: Seeing good traction across categories in July
items.quote: Yes. So we are seeing good traction in month of July for all categories. Basically, that's what I mentioned.

items.statement: Writing Instruments export pipeline strong; Middle East routes open post-conflict
items.quote: We have a good pipeline of orders and now things seem a little better also after the Middle East war has now -- is almost over. So the trade routes are now pretty open. There are no shipping delays, so I think that should definitely help the business.

items.statement: Glassware grew 50% YoY in Q1; steel flask production starts Nov-Dec; mechanical pencil launched
items.quote: Within the Consumerware category, the glassware business delivered a solid growth of 50%, driving the overall growth of the segment.

items.statement: Opalware utilization at 80-85%; new glassware facility at 65% efficiency, targeting 85%
items.quote: So Jay, basically, in the glassware segment, it's still in the negative. So there is a loss in the quarter for that particular segment, which has dragged the profitability a little bit, but which was expected. As I had mentioned that this year is we are building capacity, and we are at about 65% efficiencies at this point of time, which ideally, we would want it to be upward at 85%.

items.statement: FY26 capex ~INR100 cr: INR40-50 cr for steel flask, rest maintenance
items.quote: So capex for this financial year is majorly going to be the steel flask, which is in the tune of about INR40 crores to INR50 crores, which is the new capex, which is going to happen. And otherwise, it's just maintenance capex. So it will be around INR50 crores- INR60 crores. So about INR100-odd crores for the year.

items.statement: Glassware plant full capacity revenue potential INR200-250 cr; expects to reach INR200 cr by FY27
items.quote: INR200 crores to -- it depends again on the product mix, but it anywhere starts from about INR200 crores to INR250 crores.

items.statement: Steel flask plant targeting 5x asset turn; expects full utilization in first year despite BIS
items.quote: Yes, of course. So I think steel flask as a category would be about 5x asset turn is what we are looking at in this category.

items.statement: General trade 75.8% of revenue; online 10.4%; modern trade 5.4%; exports 8.4%
items.quote: General trade stays the largest revenue contributor at 75.8%, followed by growing share from the online segment at 10.4%. Modern trade and exports contributed 5.4% and 8.4%, respectively.

items.statement: Writing Instruments exports: Middle East, Russia, Latvia, some US (5-7% of exports)
items.quote: Majorly, it's still Middle East, Russia, Latvia, a little bit from the U.S. We will not be much hit by the tariffs, though, because the orders are still in place, but -- and our exposure is limited.

items.statement: Aggressive pricing by competitors prevented April price hike; new entrants in opalware
items.quote: But unfortunately, we were unable to do that this year, given that there was very aggressive pricing by a lot of competition for this quarter to try to gain traction in sales.

items.statement: Margins peaked in some categories; must innovate and expand channels to sustain growth
items.quote: I think for certain categories, we have peaked, and we will now have to innovate and probably expand into the other channels of growth because, as I said, we are not seeing very great demand in the general trade channel.

items.statement: Energy costs up due to rate change in Daman; wages increased
items.quote: So our energy costs, if you see have gone up for the year because there was a rate change in Daman specifically, where the energy rate went up. The wages have gone up as well.

items.statement: Channel inventory improved vs last year; collections better in Q1
items.quote: Yes. I think it's better than before. I wouldn't say it's the best because, again, we saw a great quarter last March for Consumerware specifically, but again, having slowed down demand this year, this quarter again in terms of the secondaries also, there would be a certain amount of inventory, but it's still much better than what it was last year.

items.statement: Wim Plast merger underway; swap ratio 0.86; completion in couple of months
items.quote: It's not a complicated merger. It is just -- we needed some permissions from SEBI. And I think that's already come and now we are in the phase of merging.

items.statement: No acquisition targets currently; previous target off table after due diligence
items.quote: Yes, yes. So it was definitely off the table. So there is nothing on the table at this point of time in terms of any acquisition.

items.statement: Consumerware revenue mix 69%; Writing Instruments 14%; Furniture 17% in Q1
items.quote: Our revenue mix for the quarter comprised 69% from the Consumerware segment, 14% from the Writing Instruments and balance 17% from the Moulded Furniture and Allied Products.

items.statement: Writing Instruments segment revenue INR74 cr vs INR83 cr YoY; Unomax highest margin line
items.quote: Writing instruments continued to face challenges in terms of export demand slowdown, which got further impacted by a slowdown in our domestic sales. Hence, the segment revenue stood at INR74 crores against INR83 crores in quarter 1 last year.

items.statement: Furniture revenue ~INR90 cr; premiumization underway; expects better Q2 on festive demand
items.quote: Coming to the furniture business. The performance remains subdued with revenue of about INR90 crores. The performance is in line with the industry trends.

items.statement: Export uncertainty due to geopolitical risks; competitive intensity rising across categories
items.quote: But yes, it's a very crazy world out there. I don't know what's going to happen in the next few months. But right now, it all looks okay. It looks good.

items.statement: Employee cost increase mainly from glassware plant hiring
items.quote: So employee is majorly due to the glass business because we had started manufacturing, so we employed new people. So I think that is just because of that reason.

items.statement: Guided for good double-digit value growth for the remainder of FY26 and EBITDA margin around 7% for the rest of the year
items.quote: We do believe that for the remaining part of the year, we'll have good double -digit value growth. And from a profitability perspective, we should be in this zone of 7% for the rest of the year as well.

items.statement: Targets 100-150 bps annual EBITDA margin improvement over the next 4-5 years, with mature brands reaching mid-teens EBITDA margin
items.quote: We do believe from a next 4 to 5-year view that some of our larger brands will surely be in the mid -teen kind of EBITDA range.

items.statement: Early monsoon onset impacted sunscreen category in June, dragging company-level growth by ~200 bps
items.quote: So honestly, there is -- at a company level, I would say the impact of sunscreen growth is about 200 basis points.

items.quote: Focus categories which contribute now already to about 80% of our revenues, have grown in double digits.

items.quote: From a direct outlet reach perspective, we've gained by 50%. Nielsen also is showing a growth of 20% in terms of our distribution numbers and modern trade offtakes are also healthy.

items.quote: We have Yatish who has joined us as Chief Business Officer, and comes with 17 years of experience across Unilever and Flipkart, go od offline/online exposure, joins us to lead the business teams across online and offline systems

items.quote: Working capital continues to be negative.

items.quote: We continue to look at potential acquisition opportuni ties, which could be portfolio additive in nature in the areas which we feel are strong growth hypothesis areas for the

items.quote: We believe that by '28 itself, this is going to be a INR17,000 crores category. By 2030, this should be more than INR20,000 crores category, of which lip should be the largest sub segment.

items.statement: Gross margin improved 48 bps YoY; A&P spend for mature brands expected to settle at 27-28% of sales over next few years
items.quote: On the A&P trajectory, we believe over the majority of brands, this number should settle around 27%, 28% for brands, right, as they sort of grow over the next few years.

items.statement: Competitive intensity high and increasing in young brands segment; large players repositioning with active ingredient and science-based plays
items.quote: Competitive intensity, I would say, is high and has been increasing. But I think that's a reality that we are fairly tuned into.

items.statement: Quick commerce market shares higher than e-commerce shares in almost all focus categories; channel transition to QC is margin-accretive vs e-commerce
items.quote: In almost all of our focus categories, our quick commerce shares are higher than our e -commerce shares, which is where it's a very healthy sign.

items.statement: Launched anti-pollution factor (APF) technology in Aqualogica sunscreens providing 80% protection from external pollutants; commercialized shampoo formula beating leading global brand in blind tests
items.quote: We have been able to launch in Aqualogica called APF, which is an anti-pollution factor technology that provides 80% protection from external pollutants.

items.statement: South India underpenetrated; focusing on vernacular communications and insighting to improve regional share indexing
items.quote: Honestly, being a North-based company, we believe that we haven't leveraged on the South opportunity as well and as we should have.

items.statement: No strategic interest in beauty devices/beauty tech; media articles on this had no company backing
items.quote: No, currently, no strategic interest in that area. The article did not have any backing from the company and its spokesperson.

items.statement: Target to double key count to 4,000 by FY29
items.quote: We have a clear and ambitious trajectory focused on doubling our key count to 4,000 by Financial Year '29.

items.statement: Bangalore Phase-1 hotel with 235 keys on track to open by end of Q4 FY26
items.quote: Bangalore Phase-1 continues to be progressing very well, on track to achieve the opening of hotel with 235 keys by end of Q4 Financial Year '26, that is by end of Q4 this financial year.

items.statement: Bangalore Phase-2 expansion of 273 keys design completed, construction to start end of current year
items.quote: We have already completed design phase of Bangalore Phase 2, the additional rooms to be added to this existing hotel that we are now going to open in Q4 of '26. This expansion of 273 keys will make it one of a very large big box hotels in our portfolio.

items.statement: Guwahati hotel design completed, 250 rooms, construction to start end of current year
items.quote: We have also completed the design work of Guwahati Hotel, located Downtown Guwahati, and we are set to add 250 rooms to our portfolio.

items.statement: Kaziranga project 116 keys, construction to start by September this year
items.quote: And we intend to initiate construction of 116 key Kaziranga project by September of this year.

items.statement: Capex target of Rs. 1,800-2,000 crores over next three to four years maintained
items.quote: Yes. Hi, Raghav. Yes, we are on track to what we had shared in the analysts meet.

items.statement: Submitted bids for NCR and Bihar greenfield opportunities totalling 500-odd rooms, results by August end
items.quote: Juniper has also submitted bids for NCR and Bihar greenfield opportunities, which will be opened by August end. I hope that we will be able to be successful in these two bids and they will become significant part of our going forward growth trajectory.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 EBITDA margin expanded 5 percentage points YoY to 27% growth, Rs. 86.4 crores
items.quote: Juniper achieved healthy growth of 5 percentage points in EBITDA in this quarter vis-à-vis the Q1 last year, translating into a 27% Y-o-Y growth in EBITDA to Rs. 86.4 crores

items.statement: Sustainable EBITDA margin target in the region of 40-odd-percent
items.quote: And we believe for a company like us, the sustainable EBITDA margin should be in the region of 40-odd-percent.

items.quote: Juniper portfolio also achieved a 9% growth in ARR over last year.
