items.quote: On an overall basis, in July, our ARRs would have grown by roughly 6% odd Y-o-Y.

items.statement: Underlying demand strong, ARRs growing YoY, branded hotel supply 8.4% CAGR vs demand 10.4% CAGR through FY28
items.quote: As per industry reports, branded hotel supply is expected to grow at 8.4% CAGR through FY '28, while demand is projected to outpace this at 10.4% CAGR.

items.statement: Q3, Q4 forward bookings very strong, MICE business displaced not canceled, Q2 forward bookings better than last year
items.period: Q2 FY26, Q3 FY26, Q4 FY26
items.quote: Q3, Q4 business on books is very, very strong in the bigger cities, even the smaller cities are doing very well. So, in my opinion, the business, it's been displaced, it's not been canceled.

items.statement: Lease-based occupancy at 85%, provides headroom for growth
items.quote: We have seen today the lease-based occupancy at 85%, which also provides headroom for growth to increase the occupancy over the next few quarters.

items.statement: Net bank debt to TTM EBITDA at 1.3x, gross debt Rs. 740 crores, cash Rs. 250 crores, average cost of borrowing 8.3%
items.quote: We continue to maintain a strong and healthy balance sheet with net bank debt to TTM EBITDA at around 1.3.

items.statement: Interest cost fell 21% YoY, average cost of borrowing 8.3%, expected to soften further
items.quote: On the interest cost side, interest has fallen 21% Y-o-Y, reflecting our reduced debt. Our average cost of borrowing is today around 8.3%, and we expect it to soften further given what's happening in the benchmark rates in the sector.

items.statement: ROFO integration progressing positively, expected in FY27 via share swap, non-cash
items.quote: The ROFO integration process continues to make positive progress, and we remain confident of our timelines of integration in FY '27.

items.statement: ROFO integration will be non-cash share swaps, value to be disclosed later
items.quote: As the integration process would be non-cash, these would be share swaps. And that's the manner in which they will come in.

items.statement: RevPAR growth tailwind from demand-supply gap in luxury/upper upscale segments
items.quote: Ample headroom is there to sustain RevPAR growth across industry providing continued tailwind to our pricing and profitability.

items.statement: Bangalore Phase-1 targeting Rs. 40 crores EBITDA in first year of operations (FY27)
items.quote: As far as the number is concerned, we are targeting an EBITDA of roughly around Rs. 40 crores in the first year of operations from Phase-1.

items.statement: Ahmedabad occupancy at 85% despite 59 room inventory addition
items.quote: Ahmedabad has been, as you know, we added 59 rooms to the inventory. And despite the addition, we are at 85% occupancy in Ahmedabad.

items.statement: Green energy share increased to 30% of units in Q1, contributing to energy cost savings
items.quote: As far as the current quarter is concerned, as I said, we have savings in energy costs because the share of green energy is increased to 30% in this quarter in terms of units.

items.statement: Exceptional provision of Rs. 17.1 crores for Bengaluru fire incident in April 2025, fully insured, provisions to reverse as claims received
items.quote: This is on account of an incident in Bengaluru, a fire incident in Bengaluru that happened in April 2025, and that is the provisional provision that we have taken during the quarter. We expect to receive further transfers from insurance claims. It's fully insured, and these provisions will be reversed as and when we continue to get the insurance claims over the next few quarters in this fiscal yea

items.statement: Apartment ARR growth 8-19% in Mumbai and Delhi, long-stay annuity demand robust, targeting higher occupancy via new contracts
items.quote: ARRs on apartments have also grown between 8% to 19% in Mumbai and Delhi, respectively.

items.statement: International business turned operationally profitable in Q1 FY26
items.quote: First, our international business spanning 6 countries outs ide of India turned operationally profitable in quarter 1 FY '26, marking a key milestone in our global expansion journey

items.statement: Uniware achieved annual transaction run rate of over 1 billion order items in Q1 FY26
items.quote: Uniware, our flagship platform achieved an annual transaction run rate of over 1 billion order items during the quarter, at par with the festive season quart er of FY '25, indicating consistent growth in volumes managed through our platform

items.statement: Adjusted EBITDA margin improved to 21.1% in Q1 FY26 from 16.3% in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Adjusted EBIT DA margins improved from 16.3% in Q1 FY '25 to 21.1% in Q1 FY '26

items.statement: Shipway became PAT positive in Q1 FY26 after restructuring low-margin accounts
items.quote: Shipway became PAT positive during the quarter.

items.statement: Capitalized INR1.5 crore employee expenses in Q1 FY26 for UniShip product; no major capitalization expected from Q2
items.quote: So Rajvi, we have done capitalization of near about INR1.5 crores in this quarter 1 FY '26. And the purpose of doing this capitalization is to bring that UniShip product to a terminal stage. We Unicommerce e don't anticipate to do capitalizations in the subsequent quarters

items.statement: Commercially launched payment reconciliation module UniReco in Q1 FY26 with positive early feedback
items.quote: Second, we also commercially launched our payment reconciliation module, UniReco, which enables sellers to streamline their receivables from e-commerce platforms and identify potential financial leakages.

items.statement: Launched AI-powered chatbot Loca on Shipway for post-purchase issue resolution
items.quote: Product enhancements during the quarter included launch of an AI-powered chatbot, Loca, to help brands get instant resolutions for post-purchase issues like shipment tracking, delivery delays without human intervention, along with improving user experience and expanding system integration.

items.statement: Added 88 new clients in Q1 FY26 including Ajanta Shoes, Himalaya Wellness, Rupa, Lacoste
items.quote: Third, we continue to focus on adding new clients with 88 new clients acquired in Q1 FY '26 as we continue to see strong sales momentum. Select additions this quarter include traditional as well as digital first brands such as Ajanta Shoes, Himalaya Wellness, Rupa, Lacoste, Richlook, SuperYou, Beyond Snack and Eat Better Company.

items.statement: No logo churn among top 10 Uniware clients; top 10 revenue share declining due to client base diversification
items.quote: I can confirm on this call that there have been no logo churn among the top 10 customers.

items.statement: Overlap between Uniware and Shipway client bases remains around 10%
items.quote: Our overlap continues to be in the similar ballpark of 10%, which we reported in the last quarter.

items.statement: Uniware effective rate around INR1.1-1.2 due to lower minimum guarantees for new-age brands and higher quick commerce/B2B volume mix
items.quote: But as of now, I would say that it's been in the similar ballpark of 1.1 as we had mentioned, 1.1 to 1.2 due to some of these initiatives that we had taken in FY '25 and the slight increase -- a larger increase in quick commerce and B2B volumes are immediate focus areas, has resulted in a slight decline as you have observed.

items.statement: Price escalation clauses introduced in new contracts since last year; benefits to accrue later in FY26
items.quote: The price escalation has been introduced on the new contracts since last year. The benefit of that will start accruing in the later part of this year as more and more contracts complete the year through FY '26.

items.statement: Shipway ARR reached INR80-85 crores in July vs INR70 crores in Q1 FY26
items.quote: Encouragingly, Shipway's ARR as of July has already exceeded around INR80-85 crores in July, up from approximately INR70 crores in quarter 1 FY '26, demonstrating a rebound and strong underlying momentum.

items.statement: International business contributes 4-5% of overall revenue
items.quote: Yes. So the international business is roughly 4% to 5% of the overall revenues.

items.statement: Shipway operates in TAM of nearly INR4,000 crores; expected to be largest growth driver among new products
items.quote: See, Shipway operates in a large TAM of nearly INR4,000 crores, Sumit. So I think there's significant headroom for growth. I think the journey has just started and Shipway can continue to tap into this large customer base of social media sellers, brands selling on their own website.

items.statement: Material decline in people costs on standalone business due to AI-driven efficiencies in product development and client support
items.quote: We have realigned our investment essentially related to people costs because now with the help of AI, we are able to do things a lot faster than what we could do a year ago because of which we've been able to build a lot of people-related efficiencies, and you would see a material decline in our people costs on the stand-alone business.

items.statement: Provisioning maintained at 80%, among highest in industry
items.quote: We continue to maintain our provisioning at 80%, which we believe is among the highest in the industry.

items.statement: Collected INR 41 crores in Q1 FY26 from overdue buckets vs INR 52 crores in Q4 FY25; initiated telecalling, SMS with digital payment links, and legal actions including Lok Adalat
items.quote: You will notice in the presentation that we have collected INR 41 crores in the current quarter as well compared to INR 52 crores in Q4FY25 from the overdue buckets.

items.statement: Guiding for around 20% AUM growth for full year FY26; confident of achieving this despite evolving environment
items.quote: We are looking at around 20% as a number for the full year growth. Having said that, the environment has been evolving. And we would like to be cautious while things are still evolving.

items.statement: Expect forward flows to ease and better performance across all buckets from Q3 FY26 onwards; one more quarter of pain expected
items.quote: I think it will take one more quarter. But from third quarter onwards, we should see a better performance on all the buckets.

items.statement: Expect PPOP to turn positive in coming quarters as disbursements improve and cost rationalization continues
items.quote: However, with disbursements improving and continued rationalization in our operations on the cost side, we expect the PPOP to turn positive in the coming quarters.

items.statement: Expect normalized disbursements from September 2025 onwards; July disbursements at INR 265 crores vs INR 280 crores for entire Q1
items.quote: we have also started seeing increase in the pace of disbursements with July number alone recording disbursements of INR 265 crores against the INR 280 crores disbursed in the entire quarter of Q1.

items.statement: Expect AUM growth to resume QoQ from Q3 FY26 onwards (second half of fiscal year)
items.quote: Growth in the AUM. Yes, yes. That's right.

items.statement: New normal credit cost for microfinance industry on BAU basis estimated at 2.5% to 3%; digital collections now trending at ~14% vs 3-4% previously
items.quote: For the current year, it is still evolving. So I would not like to reflect on that. But on a BAU basis, the new normal for microfinance industry should be anywhere between 2.5% to 3% in terms o f credit cost.

items.statement: Employee count reduced from 19,808 to 18,382 in March to 15,574 in June 2025; merged 81 branches; will be watchful on backfilling attrition based on productivity metrics
items.quote: if you look at our last 3 quarters, we were at 19,808 as number of employees went down to 18,382 in March, went down to 15,574 in June of '25.

items.statement: Board initiated CEO succession process; expects conclusion in next 30-45 days; will consider both internal and external candidates
items.quote: I think the Board has been looking at this particular thing in great detailand I think they have initiated the process some time back. So in next 30 to 45 days, we should be able to get this concluded.

items.statement: Implemented Guardrails 2.0 credit rules from January 2025 (ahead of peers from April 2025); increased cooling-off period between loans from 6 to 12 months; 85% loans for 2-year tenure, 15% for 12-18 months
items.quote: We have implemented stricter guardrails 2.0 credit rules from January 2025, while I think some of the peers would have taken up this starting April 2025.

items.statement: New disbursements post-January 2025 performing extremely well: Q4 FY25 disbursements at 95.6% current book, FY26 disbursements trending at ~100% current book
items.quote: the current book for whatever was disbursed since January in the last financial year was at 95.6%, whereas if you look at the current year disbursements, it is trending at around 100% in terms of current book.

items.statement: 50% of existing and dormant customers eligible for fresh loans under stricter norms; 85% of eligible have <INR 1 lakh exposure, 65% have >2 year vintage
items.quote: We have disclosed in our presentation about 50% of our existing customers and some dormant customers are eligible for fresh loans as per our stricter internal lending norms.

items.statement: Enhanced customer journey with liveliness checks, compulsory geotagged house visits, welcome calling, e-signing, 90-day bank statement requirement, upfront CB checks
items.quote: We have done multiple enhancements in the customer journey, including introduction of liveliness checks at various stages, compulsory house visits, which are now corroborated with technology in terms of validation and through geotagging.

items.statement: Spandana-plus-3-or-more lender overlap borrowers contributed ~30% of GNPA historically; 13% of Spandana customers over 30 dpd; 96% of remaining book current
items.quote: the Spandana plus 3 borrowers over a period of time have contributed about 30% in our GNPA in the past. So they definitely are far more delinquent compared to the rest of the buckets.

items.statement: NII declined 43% YoY to INR 113 crores; yield on portfolio fell to 19.4% from 20.7% QoQ due to interest reversals; net loss of INR 360 crores including INR 131 crores technical write-off
items.quote: The net interest income for the quarter was INR 113 crores over INR 425 crores reported in Q1 of last year. NII was lower by 43% over the last quarter.

items.statement: AUM dropped 27% QoQ to INR 4,958 crores due to low disbursements; confident of quick quality book growth once environment stabilizes
items.quote: AUM at the end of Q1 was at INR 4,958 crores, a drop of 27% quarter -on-quarter. As you all understand, AUM is an outcome of disbursements, and we are confident once the operating environment stabilizes, and our systems are rolling, we will be able to grow a quality book very quickly.

items.statement: Microfinance industry gradually moving towards stability; will meet existing customer working capital needs if they comply with credit rule engine
items.quote: While we'll continue to maintain a cautious stand, we are also aware of the need of our customers for the working capital and all these requirements shall be met as long as the customers comply with the credit rule engine that we have set out

items.statement: Joint liability model weakened but still needed for right operating cost and servicing large customer base; digital collections rising to ~14% from 3-4%
items.quote: While the joint liability has weakened, it is still something that needs to be used as a tool to have right operating cost and to have the right model in terms of servicing the large customer base, which microfinance kind of services.

items.statement: Worked with credit bureaus on scoring models; regression analysis shows no clear pattern; planning in-house scoring model combining credit score, activity, geography nuances
items.quote: We have done a lot of analysis internally, and we have worked with even the credit bureaus to understand if there is a suitable credit scoring model or credit scores, which can be used to do the underwriting.

items.statement: NIM guidance for FY26 is 3.5% to 4%, with full-year expectation closer to 3.7%
items.quote: On the NIM, we have bottomed out now. We will be anywhere between 3.5% to 4%.

items.statement: ROA guidance for FY26 is around 1.5%, with Lakshman Rekha of 1.5% ROA and 15% ROE
items.quote: This year also, I think on an average, we should be somewhere around 1.5%. That was my guidance, and we will reach there.

items.statement: Credit cost guidance for FY26 and through FY30 is less than 50 bps; GNPA <2%, NNPA <1%
items.quote: General gu idance on the asset quality has always been that GNPA will be less than 2%, NNPA will be less than 1% , and credit cost will be less than 50 basis points

items.statement: CD ratio guidance revised to 85-90% from previous 80-85%
items.quote: Previously, my guidance was between 80% to 85%. Now my guidance is between 85% to 90%.

items.statement: Loan growth expected to exceed 25% once liability franchise builds; currently 20-25% safely
items.quote: our credit growth, which is right now somewhere between 20 to 25% safely, maybe well above 25% and as our liability franchise becomes better, we will do better g rowth on asset side

items.statement: NIM maintained at 3.54% in Q1 FY26 despite rate transmission; expected to bottom out
items.quote: Despite the interest rate transmission dynamics between advances and deposits in a falling rate scenario, NIM could be maintained at 3.54%.

items.statement: Cost of funds to drop minimum 20 bps from current levels by Q4 FY26
items.quote: Broadly, the way we are looking at it, I think from the current level, a twenty basis points drop is the minimum which we can aim for is my view.

items.statement: Net advances grew 31% YoY in Q1 FY26; gold, corporate, SME each grew >30%
items.quote: On the asset side of the business, net advances grew by 31% Y-o-Y, again significantly higher than industry growth of close to 10% Y-o-Y.

items.statement: Deposit growth 20% YoY vs industry ~10%; CASA grew 13% YoY, CASA ratio 23.49%
items.quote: On the liability side and the funding base, deposit growth momentum continues to be faster than the industry - grew by 20% Y-o-Y amidst an industry growth of aroun d 10

items.statement: GNPA 1.84%, NNPA 0.66% in Q1 FY26; PCR 80.46% with PWO; INR194 cr provisioning buffer
items.quote: Regarding the asset quality metrices, GNPA and NNPA ratio for the qu arter was at 1.84% and 0.66%, respectively, as against 1.69% and 0.68% for Q1

items.statement: Slippages INR136 cr in Q1 FY26, INR25 cr already recovered; SME slippages due to 3-4 accounts
items.quote: If you look at it, our slippage in June 24 was INR103 crores, and now it is INR136 crores. Out of the INR136 crores, already INR25 crores recovered.

items.statement: Unsecured retail portfolio only 3% of book; slippages in unsecured PL, MFI, cards not significant
items.quote: Broadly, I can tell you that our unsecured portfolio is around 3% of the overall book. Yes, slippages have increased in the three businesses, which is unsecured personal loan, MFI, a little bit of credit cards.

items.statement: CBS migration to Flexcube completed in May with 50+ surround systems; 4 data centres built
items.quote: we have an overhaul of the entire technology ecosystem in the bank, se tting up 4 data centres, building new core banking, which we just went live in the month of May along with 50- plus different surround

items.statement: Scale phase of SBS 2030 to start FY27; sustain and build phase ends beginning FY27
items.quote: As I have told in the past that as a part of our SBS vision, our sustain and build phase is expected to get over by beginning of FY '27. The real scale phase, which is the most ex citing part of the journey is going to start from FY '27 beginning

items.statement: Gold loan yield target ~11.8%; higher-yielding gold business to grow as LAS reclassified
items.quote: From that perspective, I think we should not see a fall in yield in our gold loan. I think we should be somewhere around 11.8% in that range we will target.

items.statement: Cost of deposits rose 5-6 bps in Q1 due to bulk deposits taken late in Q4 and repricing of maturing long-term deposits
items.quote: This has primarily contributed to a five - six basis point increase in cost of funds.

items.statement: Incremental cost of bulk deposits and CDs improving; deposit costs to drop from Q2/Q3
items.quote: Our incremental cost for the last quarter, either in term/ CDs or it is on bulk deposits, you are absolutely right-we are doing better off. What it means is Q2, Q3 onwards, we will start seeing a drop in our deposit costs.

items.statement: Average LCR ~123%, NSFR ~120%; CD ratio ~92% in Q1 FY26
items.quote: Average LCR for the quarter has been around 123%. NSFR ratio is around 120%.

items.statement: FCY borrowings, CDs to support liability for 1-2 more years while retail franchise builds
items.quote: Hence, last year, we did depend on FCY borrowings, CDs, and to that extent this support will be required for another 1 or 2 years.

items.statement: New RBI circular on loan against securities may require reclassification; LAS ~INR2,000 cr
items.quote: Our retail portfolio, what we show also includes loan against securities, where gold is collateral security. These loans, based on the recent RBI circular, we may have to do differently.

items.statement: Core fee income 14-15% of total income; non-interest income 17-19% (ex-PSLC)
items.quote: Core fee income is around 14% to 15%. We do not reckon the PSLC income as the core income.

items.statement: Global trade uncertainty, US tariffs, potential rate cuts factored at 25 bps in H2 FY26
items.quote: Everybody says that there is a reasonable chance of one rate cut somewhere between September to November 25. If that plays out, we have factored that in.

items.statement: Other liabilities spike of INR2,600 cr on 30 June due to one-day reconciliation lag with RBI
items.quote: The other liability, what we are talking about is the INR2,600 crores tha t you see on 30 June is transitionally balanced. Because the reconciliation happens with a one-day lag and then it gets adjusted with our balance with RBI

items.statement: Net debt expected to increase by Rs. 400-500 crores by end of FY26 for project funding
items.quote: By the end of FY '26, we may probably have addition in the net debt to the extent of around Rs. 400-500 crores.

items.statement: Net debt-to-EBITDA expected to remain below 1.0x despite debt increase
items.quote: It will translate into Net debt-to-EBITDA of still less than 1 .0x I believe.

items.statement: Plan to add ~1,000 brownfield and 500 greenfield beds during FY26
items.quote: We expect to add approximately 1,000 brownfield and 500 greenfield beds.

items.statement: Trial runs initiated at 160-bed brownfield tower at Max Mohali
items.quote: Trial runs have already been initiated at the new 160-bed brownfield tower at Max Mohali.

items.statement: Board approved agreement-to-lease for 130-bed built-to-suit hospital in Dehradun, commissioning by end of 2028
items.quote: The new facility is expected to be commissioned by the end of 2028 and will primarily focus on advanced oncology services, including radiation therapy, which is presently missing at our Max Dehradun facility.

items.statement: Executed binding term sheet to divest Chitta and Anoopshahr hospitals for Rs. 40 crores, completion by September 2025
items.quote: we have executed a binding term sheet to divest Chitta and Anoopshahr hospitals for Rs. 40 crores, with completion expected by September ’25.

items.statement: Network average occupancy at 76% in Q1 FY26, Existing Units at over 78%, base hospitals at ~80%
items.quote: Average occupancy for the Network stood at 76% compared to 75% in both Q1 last year and the trailing quarter. However, Existing Units achieved occupancy levels of over 78%.

items.statement: Occupied bed days increased 26% YoY and 4% QoQ
items.quote: Occupied bed days increased by 26% year-on-year and 4% quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: Network ARPOB Rs. 78,000, up 1% YoY and QoQ; Existing Units like-for-like ARPOB grew 5% YoY and 2% QoQ
items.quote: Average revenue per occupied bed for the quarter was Rs. 78,000, growing nominally by 1% year -on-year as well as quarter -on-quarter. For the Existing Units, like-for-like ARPOB grew by 5% year-on-year and 2% quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: Network gross revenue Rs. 2,574 crores, up 27% YoY and 6% QoQ; Existing Units like-for-like revenue growth 16%
items.quote: Network gross revenue was Rs. 2,574 crores, up from Rs. 2,028 crores in Q1 last year and Rs. 2,429 crores in the previous quarter. This reflects an increase of 27% year-on-year and 6% versus the trailing quarter.

items.statement: Network operating EBITDA Rs. 613 crores, up 23% YoY, down 3% QoQ; margin 24.9%; Existing Units margin 26.2% (+44 bps YoY)
items.quote: Network operating EBITDA stood at Rs. 613 crores, reflecting a growth of 23% year-on-year and a 3% dip quarter -on-quarter, primarily due to the impact of annual increments and additional manpower hired for new capacities.

items.statement: Existing Units EBITDA margin 26.2%, adjusted for Rs. 12 crore one-time donation margin 26.7%
items.quote: Existing Units reported an EBITDA margin of 26.2%, which is 44 basis points higher than Q1 last year. Also , adjusted for the one -time donation of Rs. 12 crores, the margin increased to 26.7% for Existing Units.

items.statement: Annualized EBITDA per bed Network Rs. 68 lakhs; Existing Units like-for-like Rs. 75 lakhs, up 7% YoY
items.value: Rs. 68 lakhs network, Rs. 75 lakhs existing
items.quote: Annualized EBITDA per bed for the Network stood at Rs. 68 lakhs. Like-for-like EBITDA per bed for Existing Units was Rs. 75 lakhs, reflecting a 7% growth year-on-year.

items.statement: Profit after tax Rs. 345 crores, up 17% YoY
items.quote: Profit after tax for th e Network was Rs. 345 crores versus Rs. 295 crores in Q1 last year and Rs. 376 crores in the previous quarter, reflecting a growth of 17% year-on-year.

items.statement: Free cash flow Rs. 389 crores; deployed Rs. 435 crores for capacity expansion and Rs. 131 crore for land at Max Vaishali
items.quote: Free cash flows for the quarter were Rs. 389 crores. We deployed Rs. 435 crores towards ongoing capacity expansion projects and facility upgrades at newer units, while Rs. 131 crore was spent towards land purchase for brownfield expansion at Max Vaishali.

items.statement: Net debt Rs. 1,755 crores vs Rs. 1,576 crores at end of March 2025
items.quote: As a result, net debt for the Network stood at Rs. 1,755 crores compared to Rs. 1,576 crores at the end of March 2025.

items.statement: International patient revenue Rs. 208 crores, up 32% YoY and 3% QoQ despite airspace restrictions
items.quote: International patient revenue reached Rs. 208 crores, registering a growth of 32% year-on-year and 3% quarter -on-quarter despite airspace restrictions and geopolitical volatility in certain regions.

items.statement: Digital revenue Rs. 744 crores (29% of total); website traffic 69 lakh sessions, up 61% YoY and 7% QoQ
items.quote: Digital revenue from online marketing activities, web -based appointments and digital lead management was Rs. 744 crores, accounting for approximately 29% of the overall revenue. Website traffic witnessed over 69 lakh sessions during the quarter, growing by 61% year-on-year and 7% quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: Oncology share ~25-26% of hospital revenue; radiation oncology bunkers coming in Dwarka and Lucknow in Q3 FY26
items.quote: some of the newer hospitals, particularly Dwarka and Lucknow , do not offer radiation oncology at this point of time, because the bunkers are not there. But in the third quarter, we are expecting the bunkers to come through in both of these hospitals.

268 beds at Nanavati in Phase 1 – We are in the advanced stages of commissioning three basements, ground to third floors, along with the seventh floor, over the next few weeks. 400 beds of Max Smart at Saket Complex – Interior and MEP fit -out works are progressing as planned, with phased commissioning expected to start towards the end of Q2 FY '26.

items.statement: Significant hiring done for new capacities (Nanavati, Mohali, Smart); doctors onboarded ahead of commissioning
items.quote: All the brownfield expansions largely offer the entire suite of services. Like I mentioned earlier, some amount of hiring that was required for augmentation of these newer hospitals has already happened, particularly at Nanavati, Mohali and Smart (Saket).

items.statement: Max@Home revenue Rs. 60 crores, up 22% YoY; 15 service lines across 15 cities, >50% repeat transactions
items.quote: Max@Home reported a top line of Rs. 60 crores, reflecting a robust growth of 22% year -on-year. It offers 15 specialized service lines across 15 cities, with over 50% repeat transactions.

items.statement: Max Lab revenue Rs. 48 crores, up 19% YoY; 55+ cities, 1,300+ collection centres
items.quote: Max Lab reported a revenue of Rs. 48 crores, reflecting a growth of 19% year-on-year. It provides services in over 55 cities through its network of more than 1,300 collection centres and active partners.

items.statement: Direct cost increase due to annual increments from April 1 and pre-staffing for brownfield trial runs; expected to moderate as percentage of revenue
items.quote: As far as direct cost is concerned, the significant majority of it is manpower cost. And on 1st of April we have increased salaries, so you get that bump up from 31st March to 1st April.

items.statement: Institutional share increased due to new beds; payor mix improvement expected to reduce direct cost percentage
items.quote: as we progress into the coming quarters, the share of the institutional beds will come down as far as these hospitals are concerned. Because you know that our strategy is to fill up the beds and then distil the payor mix.

items.statement: Acquired hospitals performance: Lucknow revenue +97% YoY, EBITDA +191%; Nagpur revenue +27% YoY; Noida revenue +14% YoY, EBITDA +32% (Rs. 24 crores)
items.quote: Lucknow has been doing very well. On a Y-o-Y basis, the revenue growth is 97% and EBITDA growth is 191%. At Nagpur, we have grown the revenues by 27% Y-o-Y and EBITDA growth is also in the same range. Noida has been a bit subdued , with around 14% Y-o-Y growth in revenue and EBITDA growth is 32% Y-o-Y.

items.statement: Expect EBITDA margin improvement in FY26 but emphasize EBITDA per bed and ROCE as better metrics; international growth and complex cases pressure margin % but increase value
items.quote: We do expect improvement. But having said that, EBITDA margin is not the correct metric to assess . Our international business is growing by 32% . It is s upposedly higher margin business in value terms, but it's a lower margin business in percentage terms.

items.statement: Vector-borne disease season delayed due to extended monsoon; typically starts when monsoon recedes
items.quote: normally the vector season happens towards the end of monsoon . T his year the monsoon has been long. So only at the end of monsoon, we will start seeing it.

items.statement: Management does not provide revenue growth guidance but commits to long-term value creation
items.quote: We don't want to sort of say that we are not giving a guidance and then give a guidance.

items.statement: Plant 6 refurbishment on track with INR 40-50 crore capex planned
items.quote: CapEx plan that we mentioned earlier is on track. So, INR 40 crores to INR 50 crores CapEx is what is planned for this plant.

items.statement: Plant 6 mechanical refurbishment in 2-3 quarters then validation; phase-wise commercialization possible in FY26
items.quote: We expect that it will be about at least maybe 2 to 3 more quarters before we do the mechanical refurbishment, and then we will enter the validation period.

items.statement: Peak revenue potential INR 1,000 crore excluding injectables, INR 1,100 crore including injectables at full utilization
items.quote: So other than injectables, with our existing plant and plant 6 capitalized, we should be able to deliver INR 1,000 crores revenue.

items.statement: Injectable facility peak utilization around INR 100 crore revenue; expansion decision when near peak utilization
items.quote: We would do that when we are very close to the peak utilization of the facility, right? We are not definitely there yet.

items.statement: CDMO growth 17.8% YoY driven mostly by volume; Trade Generics grew 25.2% YoY; Exports grew 45.4% YoY
items.quote: Our Generic Formulations CDMO vertical achieved growth of 17.8% Y-o-Y, contributing INR 160 crores in revenue.

items.statement: Gross margin expanded 71 bps YoY to 38.3%; EBITDA margin improved 70 bps to 12.6%
items.quote: The Company's gross margin expanded by 71 bps Y-o-Y to 38.3%, while EBITDA margin improved by 70 bps to 12.6%.

items.statement: Injectable gross margins higher than oral solids; pure injectable CDMO players at 18-21% EBITDA margin
items.quote: If you look at some of the pure injectable players in CDMO, they are somewhere in the range of 18% to 21%

items.statement: API price fluctuations net out over long term; limited impact as portfolio is general category not antibiotics
items.quote: Net-net, in the longer scheme of things, as you rightly mentioned, we don't see a solid impact as such, because you end up reaching where you want to reach by doing more volume when API prices are a little bit low.

items.statement: CDMO client concentration reducing; top client contribution declining consistently over 4-5 years
items.quote: We have been over the last 4, 5 years, consistently improving in reducing the contribution of our top most client.

items.statement: Trade Generics competitive intensity increasing as branded generic companies enter; cannibalization risk for them
items.quote: As more and more companies jump into the fray, the branded generic companies have sort of a dual problem to solve.

items.statement: Schedule M implementation favors organized players; Windlas invested in electronic QA/QC, infrastructure, manpower
items.quote: So these are very important things that we have been laying the foundation, and we hope that as this structural change of new Schedule M continues to implement and the government becomes more and more stricter over further years, organized companies and people who have this forward thinking should benefit.

items.statement: Exports growing in RoW markets (Asia, CIS, Africa); dossier registrations and renewals ongoing; Europe MA transfers in process
items.quote: We have been adding more and more dossiers, so getting registrations done as well as getting renewals of our existing products done in these markets.

items.statement: Trade Generics stockist network ~1,000+; aspirational target 5,000-6,000 stockists for pan-India coverage
items.quote: Q4, we have already talked about close to about 1,000-plus stockists network that we are working with.

items.statement: Depreciation decreasing due to WDV method on injectable plant; Plant 6 capex will add depreciation upon capitalization
items.quote: In initial years, we end up having more depreciation impact. And as the years pass by, the overall depreciation tends to get lower. That is what is exactly happening in our case, and that's why depreciation reduction.

items.statement: No fund raise discussed; cash accumulation continues; dividend policy ~20% of profit maintained
items.quote: Since we got listed, we have maintained compliance with our dividend policy, which is distributing close to 20% of the profit, which we have done consistently.

items.statement: Exploring M&A but no solid opportunity; open to inorganic if right fit; otherwise organic dosage form expansion
items.quote: Second thing is for M&A transactions also, we have been exploring, but we don't want to rush it. We did not come across something solid.

items.statement: Dividend of INR 12.2 crore (INR 5.8/share) paid for FY25 in August 2025
items.quote: The Board paid a dividend of INR 12.2 crores, equivalent to INR 5.8 per share to its shareholders for FY '25 in August 2025.

items.statement: Performance-linked compensation including variable pay and equity-linked compensation for talent retention
items.quote: Even on the manpower side, where we have very strong performance-linked compensation, both in terms of variable pay as well as in terms of equity-linked compensation.

items.statement: Indian pharma market grew 9% YoY with 1% volume growth in Q1 FY26; Windlas grew 19.9% YoY
items.quote: The Indian pharmaceutical market registered a Y-o-Y growth of 9% in Q1 FY '26 with a modest volume growth of 1%. We delivered 19.9% Y-o-Y revenue growth for the quarter.

items.statement: No US tariff impact as business predominantly domestic; insulated from international trade issues
items.quote: No, not at all. In fact, I think that one of the good things about us is that most of our business is in domestic market.

items.statement: 10th consecutive quarter of record revenue; EPS INR 8.4 (30% YoY); Revenue INR 210 crore, EBITDA INR 27 crore, PAT INR 18 crore
items.quote: On the back of performance momentum seen consecutively across last 10 quarters, we delivered another quarter of consistent performance with revenue of INR 210 crores, EBITDA INR 27 crores and PAT INR 18 crores.

items.statement: Acquired Sky Gate Hospitality (Biryani by Kilo, Goila Butter Chicken), increased stake to 86.13%, 105 outlets
items.quote: I am pleased to announce that we have concluded the acquisition of Sky Gate Hospitality, which runs 'Biryani by Kilo' and 'Goila Butter Chicken' brands and increased our stake to 86.13% subsequently.

items.statement: Plan to open 100-110 net new KFC stores in FY26
items.quote: We are on track to open approximately 100-110 net new stores.

items.statement: Slowing Pizza Hut organic expansion in FY26
items.quote: In the current financial year, we are planning to slow down our organic expansion of Pizza Hut stores openings.

items.statement: Launching New York Fries, Tealive, Sanook Kitchen next quarter
items.quote: We are also in the process of launching our three new international brands i.e. New York Fries, Tealive and Sanook Kitchen in the next quarter.

items.statement: KFC SSSG stabilized at negative 0.7%, online SSSG positive
items.quote: We have seen good progress with KFC SSSG after multiple quarters, with SSSG stabilizing at negative 0.7%.

items.statement: Pizza Hut SSSG negative 4.2%, ADS recovered sequentially to INR 33,000
items.quote: SSSG came in at negative 4.2%, and efforts are underway to stem the decline.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin 15.1%, down due to lower ADS and marketing investments
items.quote: Reported EBITDA came in at INR 205 crore with EBITDA margin at 15.1%. The slight dip in margins was due to deleverage from lower ADS year-on-year and investments in marketing and promotion in the quarter.

items.statement: KFC brand contribution margin 15.5%, down due to lower gross margin, higher delivery costs, ADS deleverage
items.quote: The brand contribution margin came in at 15.5% for Q1 FY26 due to lower gross profit margin, higher delivery and aggregator costs and deleverage on lower ADS.

items.statement: Pizza Hut slight negative brand contribution in Q1 FY26
items.quote: The brand had a slight negative brand contribution in the current quarter.

items.statement: Own brands brand contribution margin declined to 6.7% due to Sky Gate consolidation
items.quote: Brand contribution margin from own brands declined to 6.7% owing to this consolidation and dilution from Sky Gate portfolio of brands.

items.statement: International brand contribution improved to 16.7% on better Thailand gross margin
items.quote: Brand contribution improved to INR 72 crore, representing 16.7% margins on the back of better gross margin performance in the Thailand business.

items.statement: Gross margin impacted by raw material inflation in cheese, flour, edible oil and GST on rent
items.quote: There was also a small impact f rom the increase in raw material prices of ch eese, flour, and edible oil. A change in GST applicability on rent has also led to an increase in rental

items.statement: Aggregator and delivery costs increased structurally due to high off-premise salience
items.quote: Further, high saliency of off-premise sales across the 2 key brands, i.e. KFC and Pizza Hut, led to higher aggregator and delivery expenses. These costs have increased on a structural basis across the industry, and the impact will continue for the year.

items.statement: Expect gross margin and brand contribution margin improvement from Q3 FY26 as promotions optimized
items.quote: Within the next quarter, basically Q3, we will start to see the gross margin improving as well as the same flowing into the brand contribution margin.

items.statement: Target KFC ADS of INR 100,000 on consistent basis for full year
items.quote: Our normalized KFC target is about INR 100,000 of ADS on a consistent basis for the full year.

items.statement: Aim to turn around Sky Gate to positive brand contribution and EBITDA within 12 months

items.statement: Another INR1,200 crores needed to complete research lab, customer qualification plant and first gigafactory (1 GWh)
items.quote: So we should be required to infuse another INR1,200 crores for us to complete the research lab customer qualification plant as well as the first gigafactory with about 1 gigawatt hour capacity.

items.statement: Tubular battery plant at Chittoor commenced commercial production in July, will reach full capacity of 150,000 batteries/month in 2-3 months
items.quote: In July, we have commenced our commercial production. So it will take generally about 2 to 3 months to reach its full capacity. Thereafter, it will run at its stated capacity of about 150,000 batteries per month.

items.statement: Recycling plant refining operations ramping up well; battery breaking operations expected to come online around October-November
items.quote: We expect that the battery breaking operations to come into full swing sometime around October-November times, provided all the trial runs go as per our expectation.

items.statement: Customer qualification plant and research lab expected functional by end of FY26; gigafactory construction started, targeting FY27 end for commencement
items.quote: We expect the customer qualification plant and the research lab to be functional by the end of this financial year and -- or maybe research lab could be ready by end of this calendar year itself.

items.statement: OEM demand robust with 4-wheeler OEM volumes up 12-13% YoY, 4-wheeler aftermarket up 5% YoY, 2-wheeler volumes up 5-6% YoY
items.quote: And during the current quarter, the OEM demand was robust along with the aftermarket growth in the 4-wheeler as well as 2-wheeler segments.

items.statement: Export volumes declined 7-8% YoY due to weakened far-off markets and tariff challenges; expect challenge for next 1-2 quarters
items.quote: And export volumes is where we faced challenge during the current quarter, where there was a degrowth compared to the previous year by about 7% to 8%.

items.statement: Telecom Lead Acid volumes degrew ~30% YoY; Industrial UPS volumes grew ~15% YoY; overall industrial Lead Acid volumes down 3-4% YoY
items.quote: With this, it's kind of negated, there is no growth on the overall volumes. In fact, if you look at 30% degrowth and 15% growth in UPS, it will result in a degrowth of industrial Lead Acid volumes by about 3% to 4%.

items.statement: Lithium pack volumes registered substantial growth, crossed 100 MW sales to telecom sector, protecting >50% market share
items.quote: We have crossed almost 100 megawatt of sale of lithium packs to the telecom sector, resulting in the overall market share in telecom being protected over and above 50% that we have been having even in the Lead Acid side.

items.statement: EV side of New Energy business slowed due to lower OEM demand for packs and chargers; expect revival in coming quarters
items.quote: whereas the EV side of the business has slowed down during the current quarter owing to a lower demand from the OEMs that we are supplying to, both on the packs as well as the charger side of it, and we expect this demand to revive in the coming quarters.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin at 11.5% (11.7% adjusted for lithium revenues); subdued due to material costs, power/employee cost increases, warranty provisions, and higher trading mix (23% vs 19% YoY)
items.quote: The margins of the current quarter were subdued, owing to the material cost challenges we have seen even in the previous year. While on a stand-alone basis, they're at about 11.5%.

items.statement: Antimony prices stabilizing; no immediate price hike possible due to competitive scenario; expect margin improvement from Q2 as power issues resolve and tubular plant ramps up
items.quote: As far as antimony is concerned, I think it is now getting stabilized at a given level. As you know, we have taken some price increase in Q4 and thereafter, the competitive scenario doesn't permit us to think about a further price increase immediately.

items.statement: Expect margin trajectory to move upward from current levels; Q1 and Q4 of last year were worst; recycling/refining operations starting to help
items.quote: I think with recycling, refining operations have started. So battery breaking operations will take another two, three months to start because the ramp-up process is currently on. So I hope we will only move upward in terms of the margin trajectory.

items.statement: No pricing actions taken in Q1; last price increase was in Q4 FY25; LFP cell prices may have bottomed at $50 and could move up due to raw material uptick
items.quote: Recently, we have seen some uptick at the raw material level, but we are yet to see that translating into price change at the cell level. But I think our reading at this point of time is that there could be a possible upward movement at the cell prices also.

items.statement: Trading revenue mix increased to 23% in Q1 from 19% YoY due to tubular factory starting production only in July; will normalize as manufacturing ramps up
items.quote: What used to be a 19% in last year, the trading revenue in this current quarter is about 23%. That also kind of have shown a bit of a dilution on the EBITDA margin.

items.statement: New Energy revenue at INR122 crores driven by strong storage (telecom) volumes; EV side slowed due to lower OEM demand
items.quote: As far as the overall New Energy business is concerned, the revenue was about INR122 crores, where it was aided by a very strong growth on the storage side volumes particularly the telecom sector.

items.statement: No change in number of OEM customers; 4-wheeler OEM growth driven by higher allocation on existing platforms, not new customers
items.quote: The number of customers that we are operating has not changed during the current quarter, but only some of the allocation that we have received on some of the platforms that we are participating has increased.

items.statement: Unorganized market remains at 10-15% in both 4-wheeler and 2-wheeler aftermarket; no sharp reduction seen over last 3 years
items.quote: It still remains around 10% to 15% range, depending on which product segment that we are talking about. Both in 4-wheeler and 2-wheeler, I think it is around that 15% mark.

items.statement: GST rationalization from 28% to 18% for Lead Acid would bring parity with lithium (18%), reduce working capital burden, and help organize scrap collection if scrap GST also reduced
items.quote: From a traditional Lead Acid Battery point of view, it puts Lead Acid Batteries on par with lithium because today, lithium's GST is about 18%, whereas Lead Acid Batteries are subjected to 28%.

items.statement: GST reduction on finished batteries (28% to 18%) would reduce working capital burden as raw materials already at 18%; scrap batteries currently at 18% GST
items.quote: Number two, the raw materials that we are sourcing are also taxed at 18%. To that extent, the overall working capital burden that will be there on the company also will come down.

items.statement: Lead Acid Battery market estimated at ~INR40,000 crores; expect overall growth of ~10% including international markets for reasonable period
items.quote: Our estimate was around INR40,000 crores. And I think we know that there is downside risks as far as storage is concerned because we are seeing what's happening in the telecom side.

items.statement: ~150-200 engineers working on cell technology and design; 3-pronged talent approach: global talent, expat recruitment, partnerships
items.quote: So today, we have roughly about 150 to 200 engineers working on these spaces on cell technology and design and a few others working on the back side.

items.statement: Export outlook uncertain for FY26 due to tariff challenges and supply chain issues; hope to revive growth by expanding into new markets in second half
items.quote: Exports, while we expect to grow more around 15%, but this year, I think it may be subdued given the supply chain challenges that we are seeing across the market because of these tariffs and all.

items.statement: Power cost issues expected to resolve by end of Q2 or beginning of Q3; good developments happening currently
items.quote: Yes, I'm expecting this to get resolved by end of the current quarter or at the latest by beginning of Q3. I think, there is some good developments that are happening right now.

items.statement: Outlook: Industrial UPS 5-6% growth, 4-wheeler aftermarket 6-7%, 2-wheeler aftermarket 10-11%, exports targeting 15% but may be subdued this year
items.quote: Whereas when it comes to the automotive aftermarket, both 2-wheeler and 4-wheeler, 4-wheeler, we expect the aftermarket to grow around 6% to 7% kind of a number. And whereas the 2-wheeler might grow around 10% to 11%.

items.statement: Lithium-ion supply chain largely dependent on China for cathode, anode, electrolyte; Indian ecosystem will take time to ramp up
items.quote: See, if you are asking about the lithium batteries, the entire supply chain is clearly from China only. I think except for a few components that we expect that Indian manufacturing will start, most of the basic raw materials of cathode and anode materials, including electrolyte will start only as imports from China.

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance of 10% for FY26 and EBITDA target of approx Rs 2,100 crore
items.quote: we have given guidance that revenue will be increased by 10% and our approx. EBITDA last year was Rs. 1,900 crores, this year it will be approx. Rs. 2,100 crores.

items.statement: Aseptic packaging volume guidance revised to 8.5-9 billion packs for FY26 from earlier 10 billion
items.quote: Asepto, we had earlier given a guidance of about 10 billion packs. So, in the Q1, we have achieved about 2.3 billion packs , which is April, May, June. So, I think we will look at somewhere between 8.5-9 billion packs now.

items.statement: Total approved capex of Rs 2,000 crore; Rs 1,100 crore spent by June 30; balance Rs 900 crore to be spent in FY26 and Q1 FY27
items.value: Rs 2,000 crore total; Rs 1,100 crore spent; Rs 900 crore balance
items.quote: the ongoing CAPEX, which has been approved by the board, the total amount is about Rs.2,000-odd crores, out of which as on 30th of June, we have already spent about Rs.1,100-odd crores, balance Rs.900 crores is what is expected to be spent in the current year as well as in the Q1 of FY27.

items.statement: Aseptic packaging expansion from 7 to 12 billion packs delayed; commissioning expected in H2 FY26
items.quote: the CAPEX plans, what we had in terms of expanding the Aseptic Packaging capacity from 7 to 12 billion packs , that has got some delayed. We were expecting that to start from January, the commencement of the season for 2025 calendar. But that has not happened.

items.statement: Egypt PET resin plant achieved 75% capacity utilization in first quarter of operations
items.quote: in Egypt, we achieved close to about 75% capacity utili zation, which is very good for the first quarter of operations.

items.statement: India PET resin plant achieved 97% capacity utilization in Q1 FY26
items.quote: in India , we achieved a capacity utilization of 97% during the quarter

items.statement: Film production volume run-rate guided at ~132,000 tons per quarter for FY26
items.quote: Somewhere around 132,000 tons per quarter.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 EBITDA margin 12% vs 12.7% YoY; expects improvement from supply-side changes and tariff settlement
items.quote: On the whole, the margin for this quarter has been slightly lower . Same period last year, we had a 12.7 % EBITDA margin, but this quarter it is 12 %.

items.statement: BOPP gross value addition risen considerably post competitor plant accident; 35% margin over raw material cost
items.quote: On a gross basis, value -added, depending on the basic film, 35% margin over the raw material cost in the BOPP.

items.statement: Packaging films volume grew 6.8% YoY; packaging business volume grew 11.7% YoY; overall sales volume up 7.9% YoY
items.quote: are up by about 6.5%, close to about Rs.4,000 -odd crores, Rs.3,922 crores for the quarter, driven by a volume increase of 7.9% on a year-on-year basis, and the packaging bit has grown by about 11.7% on a year -on-year basis, and I am talking about the volumes and the packaging films has grown by about 6.8% during the Q1 on a year-on-year

items.statement: Flexible packaging volume grew 7.4% YoY; liquid packaging volume grew 18% YoY; holographic films declined 5% YoY
items.quote: this quarter for Flexible Packaging business, the volume grew by about 7.4% on a YoY basis. For Liquid Packaging, as I said, they grew by 18%. And Holographic Films, they degrew by about 5%.

items.statement: BOPET margins bottomed out but checked by higher imports from Southeast Asia and China
items.quote: BOPET margins had improved in India. But in India, we are seeing higher imports from Southeast Asia and China also. So, I think that keeps the prices in check currently.

items.statement: Government mandate for 30% recycled content in rigid packaging and 10% in flexible packaging driving recycling investment
items.quote: given the government initiative that 30% of the recycled content in the Rigid Packaging and 10% in the Flexible Packaging, so that recycling capacity will come very handy to take care of the requirement of the products emanating from this government guidelines.

items.statement: Exports from Mexico to US covered under USMCA with nil duty; provides edge over other countries facing US tariffs
items.quote: a large part of our exports from Mexico to US are covered under USMCA and there is a nil duty as of now. And if that remains so, that will ultimately give us an edge over the other countries who were selling to US.

items.statement: US tariffs on Indian packaging exports higher than expected at 25% secondary tariff; expects resolution or deadline extension
items.quote: the tariffs announced by US on Indian products are higher than expected, especially the secondary tariff of 25%.

items.statement: New investments (Aseptic, WPP bags, recycling) expected to add Rs 3,000 crore revenue and Rs 600 crore EBITDA at 85% utilization
items.value: Rs 3,000 crore revenue; Rs 600 crore EBITDA
items.quote: by a reasonable estimate, we expect that these can add up to Rs.3,000 crore s of additional revenues at a reasonable 85 % capacity utilization levels and should give us at about Rs.600 crores of EBITDA

items.statement: SRF, Nahar, and others adding BOPP capacity in India; risk of overcapacity in 3 years if margins stay high
items.quote: SRF is adding in India. Then you have one or two other players, who are adding BOPP in India. So, BOPP which has become a big void, so I think Nahar is doing it and one more was there. Three players are there in --

items.statement: Tariff uncertainty causing customer stocking and muted North America demand; expects settlement in next two quarters
items.quote: before the anticipation of the tariff, the customers had already stocked the films and all that. So, we saw hesitation on the customers to give more orders till they are clear as to how the tariffs are going to settle. So, there has been an unsettling impact because of the tariff. And that is why in the quarter, the demand in the North American market remained a bit muted.

items.statement: Nigeria plant underperformed due to 19% US tariff and customer pre-stocking; expects recovery in next couple of quarters
items.quote: Nigeria is the worst impacted where the impact is because of the tariff being put by US. Nigeria has finally come on a 19% tariff basis and earlier US had put similar reciprocal duties on each country, they were at 10%.

items.statement: Recycling facility in Noida (40,000 tons) to be ready by year-end; will supply pre-mixed 70% virgin/30% recycled pellets for EPR compliance
items.quote: Our facility will be ready by the end of the year. So, next year, if we have the production capability and by that time things get more crystallized in terms of how the government reacts to any underperformance in the current year

items.statement: Aseptic packaging margins significantly better than conventional packaging films (11-13% range)
items.quote: even in India in Aseptic Packaging, our margins are much better than what are there in the Packaging or the Packaging Films industry.

items.statement: No exceptional forex losses in Q1 FY26 vs Rs 180 crore in same period last year
items.quote: Again, one of the key features for this quarter is that we do not have any unforeseen in terms of exceptional losses for any foreign exchange. Last quarter, same period was about Rs.180 odd crores, but this quarter, we do not have any such exceptional losses.

items.statement: US customers pre-stocked inventory ahead of tariffs; order hesitation until tariff clarity
items.quote: before the anticipation of the tariff, the customers had already stocked the films and all that. So, we saw hesitation on the customers to give more orders till they are clear as to how the tariffs are going to settle.

items.statement: WPP bags for pet food at advanced commissioning stage; Egypt aseptic greenfield expansion likely in FY26
items.quote: The Aseptic Packaging greenfield expansion of 12 billion packs at Egypt is also likely to get commissioned in FY26 , so is the WPP bags which are used for the Pet Food industry, is also at an advanced stage of commissioning.

items.statement: Targets 10,000 boepd share after capex completion
items.quote: So P90 itself, we are expecting at least 10,000 barrels for our share.

items.statement: Total capex target INR 1,250 crore over 2-2.5 years
items.quote: So we said it was about INR 1,000 crores. It may increase by another INR 250 crores. INR1,250 crores is our targeted expenditure.

items.statement: Northeast capex INR 250 crore over next 2 financial years
items.quote: Our capital outlay for the Northeastern region for the next 2 financial years continues to be INR 250 crores, and we endeavor to complete our drilling in the Northeast within 2 years.

items.statement: Cauvery offshore 4-well program capex up to $50 million
items.quote: And by all probabilities, the total capex as estimated initially for 4 wells together, it should not exceed $50 million.

items.statement: Kharsang 9-well phase to add ~1,000 bopd by Dec 2025
items.quote: We will complete this program of 9 wells before December 2025, which we expect should add about 1,000 barrels of production per day by the end of this year.

items.statement: B-80 target production 5,000 bopd after new wells
items.quote: We are planning for a total of 5,000 barrels per day. That's our planned production for B-80.

items.statement: Dirok gas sales 20 mmscfd vs 15 mmscfd previous quarter
items.quote: Dirok gas sales for the current quarter is about 20 million standard cubic feet per day, while the offtake in the previous quarter was 15 million standard cubic feet per day.

items.statement: Northeast Gas Grid expected operational by end FY26
items.quote: Although the timeline remains uncertain, we anticipate the grid to be operational within FY'26.

items.statement: Dirok gas price realized $7.54/MMBtu vs $8.45 previous quarter
items.quote: Price realized in the current quarter is US$ 7.54 per MMBtu compared to US$ 8.45 per MMBtu in the previous quarter.

items.statement: B-80 gas price realized $11.4/MMBtu vs $12.09 previous quarter
items.quote: During this quarter, the average gas price re alized is US$ 11.4 per MMBtu compared to US$ 12.09 per MMBtu in the previous

items.statement: Kharsang 4 of 9 phase-1 wells drilled, 5th underway
items.quote: In the first phase, we plan to drill 9 development wells, of which 4 wells have been drilled to date, and drilling of the fifth well is currently underway.

items.statement: B-80 workover planned post-monsoon, new platform ~1 year
items.quote: See, that workover should not be taking more than 20 to 30 days. And then we install the platform and other things, that will take about a year.

items.statement: Cauvery PY-1 4-well drilling to start Q4 FY26
items.quote: We are embarking on planning the first well drilling before the end of this financial year, and we are trying to line up the drilling rig as well as the other long lead items.

items.statement: Raised INR 250 crore long-term loan for capex, aims debt-free in 2 years
items.quote: With internal accrual, we raised a debt capital of INR 250 crores to meet the above capital expenditure. This long-term loan will be used exclusively for our capital expenditure.

items.statement: India Ratings reaffirmed IND A, outlook revised to positive
items.quote: India Ratings has reaffirmed the rating IND A and revised the outlook from stable to positive for INR 50 crores bank loan.

items.statement: B-80 oil inventory 410,000 barrels, auction via M-Junction before Aug 31
items.quote: So we are holding around 410,000 barrels of inventory at the moment and which we have already -- this has to be through an auction process to be on a transparent basis. We have appointed M-junction to carry out the auction and the technical evaluations have been completed.

items.statement: Inventory sale expected to realize over INR 220 crore
items.quote: We should be crossing more than INR 220 crores value. That's what we believe.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA INR 35 crore vs INR 39 crore previous quarter
items.quote: EBITDA for the current quarter is INR 35 crores in the consol accounts compared to INR 39 crores in the previous quarter, excluding the adjustment for the acquisition of 40% participating interest in B-80.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA INR 27.24 crore vs INR 24.38 crore previous quarter
items.quote: Standalone EBITDA for the current quarter is INR 27.24 crores compared to INR24.38 crores in the previous quarter.

items.statement: Kharsang production 450 bopd vs 351 bopd previous quarter
items.quote: During the Q1 FY'26, the Kharsang block recorded an average production of 450 barrels per day, up from 351 barrels per day in Q4 FY'25.

items.statement: B-80 production 48,406 bbl oil, 0.37 Bcf gas vs 60,000 bbl, 0.4 Bcf previous quarter
items.quote: Production in the current quarter is 48,406 barrels of oil and 0.37 Bcf of gas compared to 60,000 barrels of oil and 0.4 Bcf of gas in the previous quarter.

items.statement: Dirok condensate 8,893 bbl vs 6,603 bbl previous quarter
items.quote: Condensate production is 8,893 barrels compared to 6,603 barrels in the previous quarter.

items.statement: Kharsang environmental clearance for 40 dev + 3 expl wells secured
items.quote: As you may recall, we have secured environmental clearance for drilling 40 development wells and 3 exploration wells in this block.

items.statement: Dirok revised FDP submitted to DGH for block extension
items.quote: The revised field development plan for the Dirok block has been submitted to the DGH, enabling the extension of the block.

items.statement: Block 19 environmental clearance received, awaiting 1-year extension
items.quote: We have received environmental clearance and are expecting the extension of the block for 1 more year to start the committed work program.

items.statement: Monsoon disruptions caused B-80 production shutdown in June-July
items.quote: Production was disrupted in mid-June 2025 due to monsoon fury, and we de-moored the FSO from the SPM for safety, considering the oil in the vessel.

items.statement: PY-3 arbitration tribunal yet to be constituted, timeline unknown
items.quote: It's not under arbitration, the tribunal is to be constituted. Once the tribunal is constituted, we'll put forward our views to it.

items.statement: Targets 8-10% overall FMCG revenue growth, 15% HPC growth, 2-3% edible oil growth for FY26
items.quote: our target is very clear that -- and I'm reasonably confident that this year, we'll be able to accomplish that, that between 8% to 10% growth we should get in the overall FMCG segment. We will expand 15% on our HPC portfolio and we will expand between 2% and 3% on the edible oils.

items.statement: Aims for 200 bps margin expansion in HPC over coming quarters
items.quote: We also anticipate a 200 basis point margin expansion over coming quarters.

items.statement: Targets double-digit EBITDA margin at company level, 8-10% FMCG EBITDA, 2-4% edible oil EBITDA
items.quote: our measure is very clear that currently, our longer -term construct of margin is 8% to 10% that we're looking at the margin overall on the FMCG side. And very clearly, we are looking at the margin construct on the edible oil between 2% and 4

items.statement: Targets INR50,000 crore revenue with 50-50 split between FMCG and edible oils, double-digit EBITDA margin
items.quote: company's aspiration is that we would like to grow our revenues to INR50,000 crores, of which INR25,000 crores should come from FMCG, INR25,000 crores should come from the edible oils and the margin should expand towards a double-digit EBITDA.

items.statement: Rural demand outpacing urban; urban showing early revival signs due to easing inflation and policy measures
items.quote: Over the past few quarters, rural markets have outpaced the urban markets. Q1 FY '26 followed similar trends. The momentum in rural demand continued and demonstrated a preference for well-established brands. The urban demand was under pressure.

items.statement: Green shoots of urban recovery visible in larger cities, food demand uptick expected
items.quote: We are seeing that very clear cut, the green shoots of some small bit of recovery, especially in the larger cities now. And the stress that we saw in a couple of quarters previously, that is tending to go away.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin 3.75%, PAT margin 2.02% in Q1 FY26
items.quote: The total EBITDA margin came in at 3.75% and the PAT margin stood at 2.02%.

items.statement: Edible oil EBITDA margin 1.78% in Q1 FY26, impacted by duty reduction and high-cost inventory
items.quote: The EBITDA margin was 1.78%. The impact on margin can be attributed to multiple reasons. Following the government's decision to reduce duties, buyers deferred procurement in anticipation of price stabilization, which weighed on the overall demand and prici ng scenario

items.statement: HPC EBITDA margin 18.7% in Q1 FY26 vs 15.7% in Q4 FY25
items.quote: Dant Kanti, our flagship herbal oral care brand, delivered robust growth during the quarter. We clocked an EBITDA margin of 18.7% versus 15.7% in Q4 '25.

items.statement: Food & other FMCG EBITDA margin 5.23% in Q1 FY26 vs 9.42% in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Our EBITDA margin was at 5.23% versus 9.42% in Q1 FY '25.

items.statement: Biscuits EBITDA margin 9.2% on INR451 crore revenue in Q1 FY26
items.quote: On the biscuits, our margin was 9% EBITDA, 9.2% margin that we had. On a INR451 crore revenue, we had a INR41 crore margin.

items.statement: Nutrela EBITDA margin 14.5% on INR140 crore revenue in Q1 FY26
items.quote: On the Nutrela side, we had INR140 crores of revenue. We had INR20 crores of EBITDA margin, where we made 14.5% margin.

items.statement: Staples revenue INR616 crore with flat EBITDA in Q1 FY26; historically 3-4% margin
items.quote: So staples, as our revenue -- Abhijeet, as I mentioned, it was INR616 crores and pretty flat in terms of EBITDA.

items.statement: Palm oil prices up 7.35% YoY, down 10.2% QoQ; expected to remain range-bound with downward trajectory
items.quote: Palm oil increased by 7.35% on a year-on-year basis and reduced by 10.2% on quarter -on-quarter basis. The palm oil prices are expected to remain range bound and downward trajectory drive n primarily by recent policy measures and market dynamics

items.statement: Amla and fruit pulp raw material costs up 20% QoQ in beverage category
items.quote: For instance, in the beverage category, the raw material costs, p articularly for amla and fruit pulp had a 20% hike on a Q-on-Q basis

items.statement: Edible oil segment revenue INR6,685 crore, up ~25% YoY; branded sales 72% of total
items.quote: For the Edible Oil segment, the segment revenue was INR6,685 crores, a year-on-year growth of almost 25%. The branded edible oil sales contributed 72% of the total edible oil sales.

items.statement: Oil palm plantation revenue doubled to INR592 crore; cultivated area 92,133 hectares, 43.4% in prime yielding age
items.quote: For oil palm plantation business, we doubled our quarterly revenue and booked INR592 crores in the oil palm plantation business. As of June 2025, the total cultivated area increased to 92,133 hectares with approximately 43.4% of the plantation falling under the prime yielding age category.

items.statement: HPC revenue INR639.02 crore; dental care INR332.18 crore, skin care INR157.21 crore, home care INR91.61 crore
items.quote: On the HPC business front, the segment delivered healthy quarterly revenue of INR639.02 crores. Within this, the revenue contribution from dental care was INR332.18 crores. Skin care was INR157.21 crores. Home care was at INR91.61 crores.

items.statement: Food & other FMCG revenue INR1,660.67 crore, down 15% YoY due to subdued premium demand and government schemes
items.quote: the quarterly revenue from Food and other FMCG segments stood at INR1,660.67 crores. Non-essential and premium FMCG categories had subdued demand during the quarter. Various government welfare schemes such as free food distribution, duty-free imports of yellow peas, seasonal impacts, elevated raw material prices and slow recovery in urban demand led to a degrowth of 15% in revenue on year-on-year

items.statement: Biscuits revenue INR451 crore, up 8.24% YoY; Doodh biscuit INR304 crore, up 15% YoY
items.quote: Elaborating on the performance of biscuits vertical, which clocked 8.24% year-on-year growth, Doodh continued to lead our portfolio, contributing INR304 crores in revenue this quarter, a 15% year-on-year growth.

items.statement: Nutraceuticals revenue INR17 crore, up 37.6% YoY; achieved positive EBITDA via manpower restructuring and e-commerce/D2C focus
items.quote: Nutraceutical marked year-on-year growth of 37.6%. Positive EBITDA in nutraceuticals was achieved through manpower restructuring as intensified focus on e-commerce and D2C maximized the use of our mega stores.

items.statement: Oil refining capacity 33.36 lakh tons at end FY25, operating at 44.85% utilization
items.quote: Our oil refining capacity as of end FY '25 was 33.36 lakh tons, operating at 44.85% utilization.

items.statement: D2C share below 1% of revenue; non-traditional channels (modern trade, e-commerce, quick commerce, D2C) total 12.5%
items.quote: Right now, it would be below 1%. It's very, very small right now. So we have got -- so for example, just to tell you on the nontraditional channels, we do about a total about 12.5% is what we do overall between the modern trade, e-commerce and quick commerce and D2C.

items.statement: Dant Kanti exported to 9 countries in Q1 FY26; strong export demand
items.quote: Also in the export market, Dant Kanti had strong demand. It was exported to 9 countries in Q1FY '26.

items.statement: Government intervention in staples (rice, wheat, pulses) via procurement and subsidized sales creating margin volatility; 35-40% of paddy production procured by government
items.quote: nearly 35% to 40% of the country's paddy production is getting procured by the government. So it has got a problem of overflow of stocks and which is ultimately finds its way to the marketplace at highly subsidized levels.

items.statement: Open to selective acquisitions if pricing sensible, brand fits portfolio and Patanjali value system; nothing serious on table currently
items.quote: So we don't mind exploring acquisition of good brands and we are quite open to that. But e very time we evaluate, we normally come up short on these sort of brand acquisition. So right now, there's nothing seriously on the card, which I could say that, yes, this is what we'll do

items.statement: Branded edible oil sales 72% of total edible oil sales in Q1 FY26
items.quote: The branded edible oil sales contributed 72% of the total edible oil sales.

items.statement: Targets 10-12% volume growth over previous year on annualized basis
items.quote: So, I think this has been outlined earlier and I believe it is to the order of 10% to 12% additional volume growth over the previous year.

items.statement: Targets 12-13% volume growth for India business for the year
items.quote: In terms of volume guidance, I think for the year, we mentioned 12% to 13%, which is in line with what additional volumes will be available to us in India, and we should be able to do that.

items.statement: ABS capacity expansion of 50,000 tons planned for FY27, remaining 50,000 tons in FY28
items.quote: So it's the same what we have mentioned earlier, I think we have spoken about FY '27 and we are looking to add 50,000 tons additional ABS in FY '28, the remaining 50,000 tons.

items.statement: Phase 1 capex of INR325-350 crores by March 2027 on track
items.quote: So regarding capex for the Phase 1, as we had mentioned earlier, we'll be spending around INR325 crores to INR350 crores by March '27.

items.statement: Polystyrene capex not included in current INR350 crore guidance; engineering study ongoing
items.quote: PS capex, as announced earlier, the engineering study is going on. Once it is completed, we'll let you know more details about it.

items.statement: India capacity for FY26 expected at 210,000-215,000 tons for all products
items.quote: With regards to capacity for FY '26, it will be in line with what we had given in the earlier investor presentation, which I think is to the tune of about 210,000, 215,000 tons for all the products that we produce in India.

items.statement: Thailand plant operating at 50-55% utilization with significant scope to increase
items.quote: It's between 50% to 55%.

items.statement: Thailand plant could increase revenue by 70-80% at peak utilization with current product mix
items.quote: Essentially, if you look at the revenue in Thailand that we have and you assume a similar product mix, you can see that we can essentially increase re venue by close to 70% to 80% additionally, right, from where we are at

items.statement: Q1 volumes highest ever at 51.8 KT standalone, up 8.1% QoQ despite early monsoon impact on appliances
items.quote: The volumes in India, we did close to around 51,000 tons, which is the highest sales ever done by the company.

items.statement: Air conditioning demand down ~30% due to early monsoon; two-wheeler and four-wheeler grew
items.quote: In fact, air conditioning has been down by about 30%. And that again has to do with kind of lower demand due to the early monsoon. The two-wheeler, in fact, has grown and four wheeler also has grown a little bit.

items.statement: ABS spreads historically stable on annualized basis despite monthly volatility
items.quote: So overall, they are in line with what have been historically there, barring certain factors which can influence, say, a month or two. But on an annualized basis, I think we are very much exactly where we have been for the last few years.

items.statement: Thailand margin expansion depends on capacity utilization and product mix optimization
items.quote: So, in terms of margin expansion in Thailand, again, like I mentioned, it is a function of capacity utilization. So, we will get some operating leverage over there.

items.statement: Specialty ABS share 60-70% of total ABS sales in India
items.quote: In terms of specialty ABS, again, we have close to 60% to 70% market -- our share of specialty ABS is about 60% to 70% within our total ABS that we sell and that continues to be the case.

items.statement: Thailand offers unique grades: bimodal rubber (MAC 50), refrigerant ABS, food-grade SAN, high-heat ABS
items.quote: There is a refrigerant ABS that we do from Thailand, which is a unique and value-added product. There are certain SAN grades that we make like a food-grade SAN, which goes into certain appliances where there is direct food contact, which has a higher margin.

items.statement: Added new customers in both Thailand and India; leveraging cross-approvals between geographies
items.quote: In terms of new customers in Thailand, yes, in fact, we have added quite a few customers in Thailand. In fact, both ways, we are adding new customers in India as well as Thailand.

items.statement: Almost no ABS exported from India; Thailand supplies to China, Japan, Korea, Vietnam, Thailand
items.quote: Almost no ABS, very little, if any.

items.statement: Medium to long-term export opportunity to EU from India as European plants shut due to high power costs
items.quote: But medium to long term, yes, there will be opportunities for export from India as well, which we are looking at.

items.statement: Hybrid power SPV to be active by year-end to reduce power costs in India
items.quote: We have signed, by the way, an SPV as already is publicly known to go into hybrid power from our current power source. So that, I think, will be active by the end of the year. So that will reduce our power cost also.

items.statement: Thailand conversion cost nearly double India's; reduction via process improvements and higher utilization, not major capex
items.quote: The conversion cost in Thailand is higher than India. And this is something that our team is working on. In terms of reducing it, it is not as straightforward as one would imagine. There is a lot of work that needs to happen in order to try and reduce that conversion cost.

items.statement: Inventories ramped up in March quarter for Thailand asset validation and INEOS agreement; reducing in Q1
items.quote: In India, again, we have, in fact, reduced those inventories in this quarter, there is a reduction between the March ending and the June ending quarter.

items.statement: Dividend of INR50-55 crores paid despite capex plans; philosophy to return cash when not immediately needed
items.quote: We do believe that if the capex requirements or the cash requirements of the company come at a specific time, and we had cash on hand, then the best use of that cash is back to the shareholders.

items.statement: No speculation on further inorganic acquisitions
